items.title: Build autonomous AI agents with Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI
items.summary: AWS shows Java developers how to build autonomous AI agents with Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI, covering tool calling, memory, resilience, multi-agent orchestration, and deployment to AgentCore.
items.why: Gives Java teams a concrete production pattern for agents on AWS, spanning tool calling, memory, resilience, and deployment.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
items.summary: OpenAI published a conversation with Sam Nickless, CEO of Gilbert + Tobin, about rethinking the law firm business with AI.
items.why: Shows how a large professional services firm is restructuring its operations around AI, a useful case study for enterprise adoption leaders.

items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.summary: TechCrunch publishes a timeline of an affair scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which it says could affect national security amid US-China AI infrastructure competition.

items.title: OpenAI Codex on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: AWS publishes a guide for enterprises rolling out OpenAI Codex to developers, using Amazon Bedrock as the model backend and covering access, governance, and cost decisions.
items.why: Outlines the access, governance, and cost decisions platform, security, and finance teams must align on before a Codex rollout.

items.title: Semantic diffing of formal policies with anti-unification
items.summary: AWS describes computing a deterministic semantic diff of formal authorization policies using an open-source anti-unification engine, so reviewers see only behavior-changing differences.
items.why: Helps teams review authorization policy changes by surfacing behavioral differences rather than cosmetic text edits.

items.title: Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
items.summary: AWS explains how to detect silent GPU data corruption in PyTorch DDP training, localize the faulty node on SageMaker HyperPod, and trigger automatic node replacement.
items.why: Gives ML infrastructure teams a way to catch silent GPU errors that could quietly corrupt distributed training runs.

items.title: Introducing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: AWS launches a Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that lets code search the web via a single signed API call, with no gateway or resources to create.
items.why: Lets developers add web search to agents and pipelines through the AWS SDK or CLI without provisioning extra resources.

items.title: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang
items.summary: The Verge reports, citing WSJ and NYT, that Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang after a second alleged extramarital affair was reported.

items.title: ICYMI: What landed for AI builders in October 2026
items.summary: AWS publishes a recap of October 2026 updates to Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and Strands, including new models, agent availability features, and clearer cost reporting.
items.why: Summarizes recent platform changes that affect agent availability, grounding, and cost tracking on AWS.

items.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers
items.summary: United Airlines has reportedly banned AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers, according to a CBS News report shared on Hacker News.
items.why: Signals that some large travel providers are restricting third-party AI agents, which affects agent-driven booking designs.

items.title: The attendee’s guide to the AWS re:Invent 2026 AI/ML track
items.summary: AWS published an attendee guide to the AI/ML track at re:Invent 2026, which includes more than 140 sessions.
items.why: It helps engineers pick sessions on AI chips, inference, agents, and agent trust for their role and goals.

items.title: Automating AWS Agent Registry updates with push-based architecture
items.summary: AWS shows how to automatically update the AWS Agent Registry using an event-driven pipeline that detects MCP server changes.
items.why: Teams running agents across accounts can keep tool metadata current without storing secrets.

items.title: How DXC Technology built a multi-model AI substrate on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: DXC Technology describes DCX OASIS, its Human+AI operating model built on a multi-model substrate in Amazon Bedrock.
items.why: It shows a pattern for separating the model layer from a governance harness that orchestrates and audits agents at scale.

items.title: Why the data center you dread might never even be built
items.summary: Many announced data center projects may never be built, adding to local opposition, permitting delays, and electricity shortages.
items.why: Infrastructure planners should expect capacity announcements to slip, making delivery timelines less reliable.

items.title: Meta is losing its longtime head of infrastructure
items.summary: Meta's longtime head of infrastructure, Santosh Janardhan, is stepping down from the role.
items.why: Leadership changes in Meta's infrastructure organization could affect the direction of its large-scale systems.

items.title: How backlash and red tape continue to slow data centers post-Blue Wave
items.summary: Local backlash, permitting delays, and electricity constraints are slowing data center projects, and many announced projects may never be built.
items.why: Engineering leaders relying on planned capacity should account for delays and cancellations in their roadmaps.

items.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth
items.summary: CoreWeave is asking customers for upfront payments and offering shorter contracts, according to its third-quarter earnings.
items.why: Shifts in GPU cloud contract terms affect cost planning and capacity commitments for AI teams.

items.title: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
items.summary: Britain's Fractile raised a $720M round, making it one of the top-funded startups building purpose-built AI chips.
items.why: Well-funded alternatives to GPUs could broaden the hardware options for AI inference and training.

items.title: Congress to call Jensen Huang in to answer for alleged Chinese spy affair
items.summary: House Republicans have asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang for a closed-door briefing about his alleged affair with a Chinese spy.
items.why: Congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's leadership could carry implications for the company and its chip supply.

items.title: Accelerating generative AI delivery with reusable assets
items.summary: AWS's Generative AI Innovation Center offers a catalog of 23 open source, production-ready reusable assets for generative AI delivery.
items.why: Teams can reuse tested RAG pipelines, document processors, and agent scaffolding instead of rebuilding them.

items.title: Retirement Savings Are Fueling the AI Bubble
items.summary: A blog post argues that retirement savings are fueling the AI bubble, linking pension and retirement investment to AI market valuations.

items.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
items.summary: Google announced the Gemini Decisions API, powered by its Gemini Decision model, for fast, calibrated multimodal decisions.

items.title: AI, activity, and outcomes in software engineering
items.summary: A linked video discusses AI's effects on activity and outcomes in software engineering, shared on Hacker News with no further detail in the feed.

items.title: Is Jensen Huang’s bad behavior more commonplace than it seems?
items.summary: An investment intel consultant says many senior industry figures know about Jensen Huang's alleged misconduct and effectively condone it.
items.why: Reputational and governance concerns around Nvidia's leadership may matter to investors and partners.

items.title: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time
items.summary: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly crossed $10 billion for the first time, up almost 50% from $6.7 billion in the prior second quarter.
items.why: Rapid revenue growth at a leading model provider signals sustained enterprise and consumer demand for AI services.

items.title: Accelerating product development with AI-driven lifecycle management (AI-PDLC) in AWS Quick
items.summary: AWS describes an AI-driven product development lifecycle using six AWS Quick agents, with human approval at each gate and handoff to coding agents like Kiro.
items.why: It offers a structured workflow for turning customer signals into prototypes and specs for coding agents.

items.title: Try Tabletop: Customizable, collaborative spaces for groups to plan, play and do more together.
items.summary: Google Labs released Tabletop, a experimental collaborative space for building itineraries, polls, and brackets, with a waitlist.

items.title: UAEF: A framework-agnostic system for closed-loop evaluation of AI agents
items.summary: AWS ML Blog describes UAEF, a framework-agnostic system that converts agent traces into one canonical format and scores them with 36 metrics across 7 dimensions.
items.why: Teams running agents across multiple frameworks can compare versions and catch regressions with one shared evaluation pipeline.

items.title: Introducing usage-based pricing for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming
items.summary: AWS Marketplace now supports usage-based metering for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming inference, with Deepgram as launch partner for speech-to-text and text-to-speech.
items.why: Engineers building live voice or streaming AI services can now bill customers per consumed usage through AWS Marketplace.

items.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
items.summary: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaGenome 2, a successor model that aims to explain how DNA changes affect different cells and the causes of disease.

items.title: Databricks’ new AI agent tells CEO Ali Ghodsi the unvarnished truth
items.summary: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi says he uses the revised Genie agent to surface problems his 12,000 employees are unlikely to report directly.

items.title: Plurai wants to help AI agents work better using the same approach that helped get self-driving cars to roads
items.summary: Plurai is working on improving AI agents by applying an end-to-end training approach similar to the one used for self-driving cars.
items.why: Engineers building agents may find the idea of training for probabilistic, unpredictable environments relevant, though the text gives few details.

items.title: Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters
items.summary: Adobe announced experimental AI features at its Max conference, including turning images into explorable 3D scenes, designing AI characters through conversation, and copy/paste-style photo editing.

items.title: Google SWE points 48 AI agents at NASA Lidar, finds unmapped Maya pyramid in 72h
items.summary: A Hacker News post describes Google SWE using 48 AI agents on NASA Lidar data that reportedly found an unmapped Maya pyramid in 72 hours.
items.why: It shows multi-agent systems applied to large geospatial datasets, though the description gives little detail on the method.

items.title: Experience the art and legacy of Dr. Esther Mahlangu
items.summary: Google AI published a piece on the art and legacy of Dr. Esther Mahlangu, with a portrait of Dr. Nontobeko Ntombela from Wits School of Arts.

items.title: OSS projects banning AI-generated contributions
items.summary: A Hacker News post links to a site listing open source projects that ban AI-generated contributions.
items.why: Maintainers and engineering leaders should note that some open source projects are refusing AI-generated code contributions.

items.title: ChatGPT Plus for veterans and servicemembers
items.summary: OpenAI reports more than 20,000 veterans and transitioning service members have claimed a free year of ChatGPT Plus.

items.title: Nvidia’s crisis has corporate governance experts reaching for the popcorn
items.summary: Corporate governance experts say nobody has seen anything like the crisis currently unfolding at Nvidia.

items.title: BotPsy: On-Device Personal Assistant with a Sub-Billion-Parameter Agentic Language Model
items.summary: BotPsy, an on-device personal assistant built on a sub-billion-parameter agentic language model, was published on Hugging Face.

items.title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
items.summary: Researchers demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices using coding-agent infrastructure with human oversight and auditable transcripts.
items.why: Shows agentic systems operating real scientific instruments over sustained periods, with audit trails for reconstructing decisions.

items.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
items.summary: EarthRecord is a benchmark testing multimodal agents on raw four-decade satellite archives from 56 sites for land-change analysis.
items.why: Existing benchmarks skip raw multi-sensor data, so this tests whether agents can handle the messier inputs real Earth observation work requires.

items.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
items.summary: TopicScope trains sparse autoencoder-based classifiers that label the topic of each token during generation, allowing topic changes mid-response.
items.why: Offers a generation-time monitoring approach beyond the two or three harmful-content classes current activation monitors handle.

items.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
items.summary: LandslideFM is a unified foundation model proposed for landslide detection, combining visual perception tasks with contextual scene interpretation.

items.title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
items.summary: A controlled study over 1,500 questions finds adding graph visualizations to prompts yields an average 1.85 F1 gain for knowledge graph question answering in vision-language models.
items.why: Gives practical evidence on when adding graph images to prompts helps or hurts, relevant to multimodal retrieval pipeline design.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning based control of Cancer Chemotherapy treatments
items.summary: A paper surveys reinforcement learning for dynamic treatment regimens and personalized cancer chemotherapy control from clinical data.

items.title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence
items.summary: The paper proposes a competence circuit framework for AI agent governance, decomposing real-world impact into discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control.
items.why: Offers a conceptual governance framing that shifts focus from limiting intelligence to controlling agent actions and knowledge boundaries.

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
items.summary: Researchers re-evaluate tabular foundation models against Optuna-tuned gradient boosting for telecom churn, scoring models on profit and calibration as well as ranking.
items.why: Challenges claims that tabular foundation models beat tuned tree ensembles when judged by business value and calibration rather than ranking alone.

items.title: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes
items.summary: SetPrint proposes a black-box method to determine whether a target LLM was derived from a source model by comparing response changes under query perturbations.
items.why: Provides a way to verify model lineage using only API outputs, relevant to provenance and licensing checks.

items.title: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs
items.summary: A controlled evaluation compares four agent architectures across 13 enterprise SOPs, holding model and tools fixed to measure cost and success trade-offs.
items.why: Gives controlled evidence on how architecture choice affects cost and success for enterprise agent workflows.

items.title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
items.summary: Physics2Weight uses LLMs to directly generate neural network weights and architectures for solving partial differential equations from governing equations.

items.title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
items.summary: The paper argues existing self-driving labs disconnect language models from physical grounding and proposes embodied science agents for learnable experimental design.

items.title: Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes
items.summary: An arXiv paper reports that monitoring one communication channel changes how learned agents route messages, while task accuracy stays high in a sender-receiver game.
items.why: Shows that observing a visible channel does not fully control agent communication, relevant to designing monitoring for multi-agent systems.

items.title: IIT Patna at "ICPR 2026 TVRID Competition on Privacy-Preserving Person Re-Identification from Top-View RGB-Depth Camera"
items.summary: IIT Patna describes its entry to the ICPR 2026 TVRID competition on privacy-preserving person re-identification using top-view RGB-depth cameras.

items.title: RBLA+: Efficient Rank-Specific LoRA Adapter Extraction for Federated Fine-Tuning with Heterogeneous Clients
items.summary: RBLA+ is a method for rank-specific LoRA adapter extraction in federated fine-tuning where clients use different LoRA ranks.
items.why: Addresses server-side aggregation when clients have heterogeneous adapter ranks, a practical issue in federated LLM fine-tuning.

items.title: BuySideFlow: A Point-in-Time Benchmark for LLM Agents in Investment Research
items.summary: BuySideFlow is a benchmark of 408 Chinese-language investment research tasks testing whether LLM agents respect point-in-time data validity.
items.why: Highlights that agents doing financial analysis must correctly enforce disclosure cutoffs, a hard data-leakage risk for production pipelines.

items.title: TrustMod-SM: A Multi-Axis Benchmark for Evaluating Trustworthiness of LLMs in Social Media Content Moderation
items.summary: TrustMod-SM is a benchmark of about 29,000 instances testing LLM content moderators on trustfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and context integrity.
items.why: Shows persistent trustworthiness gaps in LLM moderators beyond accuracy, informing evaluation before deploying them in moderation systems.

items.title: ZeroPoint: Lightweight Energy-Based Decision Model
items.summary: ZeroPoint is a lightweight energy-based decision model that adds a way to express that no option is acceptable.

items.title: Seeing Is Not Believing: Counterfactual Lesion Erasure Teaches a Small Medical Vision-Language Agent to Report Only What the Image Shows
items.summary: MedScope-4B is a small medical vision-language model trained with counterfactual lesion-erasure views to report only findings visible in the image.
items.why: Targets a known failure where medical VLMs report findings because the question names them, relevant to clinical AI reliability.

items.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
items.summary: Ask2Decide is a benchmark of 43 planning tasks testing whether LLM agents ask humans for decision-relevant missing information.
items.why: Tests a gap in agent behavior: acting on incomplete requests rather than seeking clarification, relevant to agent deployment design.

items.title: Multi-Future Drafting: Mixture Block Drafters for Tree-Verified Speculative Decoding
items.summary: The paper proposes mixture block drafters for tree-verified speculative decoding, arguing product-based drafting misallocates verification budget across futures.
items.why: Offers a potential way to improve accepted tokens per verification step in speculative decoding for faster LLM inference.

items.title: ChipOmni: A General-Purpose AI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
items.summary: ChipOmni is a knowledge-enhanced general-purpose AI agent aimed at planning, verifying, and repairing electronic design automation workflows.
items.why: Shows agents extending into chip design toolchains, relevant to engineering teams automating EDA workflows.

items.title: Understanding-First AI Engineering: Purposes, Reference Architecture, and Architectural Patterns for Human Understanding
items.summary: The paper proposes understanding-first AI engineering, treating purpose-specific human understanding as a first-class design principle with a reference architecture.
items.why: Offers architectural patterns for keeping humans understanding AI-supported work, relevant to system design and governance.

items.title: GRAP: Gender Rubric-Aware Probing for Analyzing Gender Bias in LLMs
items.summary: GRAP is a gender rubric-aware probing framework that uses logistic models to find which rubric dimensions reliably distinguish gender groups in LLM responses.
items.why: Offers a more rigorous method for measuring gender bias in open-ended LLM outputs than fixed-format probes.

items.title: APS-VLA: Action-Guided and Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: APS-VLA is a framework that learns visual token pruning from robot demonstrations to reduce inference latency in vision-language-action models.
items.why: Targets high inference latency in robotic VLA policies, a practical bottleneck for deploying them on real hardware.

items.title: Trust, but verify, audit and attribute: a human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced research results
items.summary: The paper proposes a human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced research results, focusing on auditing and attributing Lean proof translations.
items.why: Addresses verification of AI-generated proofs, where a passing check may not confirm the author's original statement.

items.title: Elicitation of the parameters of a multi-criteria sorting model
items.summary: The paper presents a rigorous procedure for directly eliciting parameters of the Non-Compensatory Sorting model in multi-criteria decision aiding.

items.title: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation
items.summary: Researchers study how intrinsic motivations such as curiosity and play shape world-model representation learning to support downstream control.
items.why: Clarifies which intrinsic reward signals yield robust world models, which may inform exploration design in agent training.

items.title: Activation-Guided Graph Retrieval for Cognitive Memory Reconstruction in Language Model Systems
items.summary: Authors propose an architecture for language model memory retrieval based on activation-conditioned availability, using a bounded traversal of an authorized memory graph before generation.
items.why: Offers a design alternative to query-relevance-only retrieval for long-lived AI systems, though the text is a specification without reported results.

items.title: Agreeing on the Answer but Not the Reason: Measurement Limits of LLM Reasoning Failure Taxonomies
items.summary: Study finds that the reported share of LLM reasoning errors in a 'Compositional Collapse' category largely depends on the measurement procedure, across twelve models and eleven languages.
items.why: Suggests failure-taxonomy comparisons across LLM papers may reflect measurement choices rather than model differences, so treat such fractions cautiously.

items.title: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents
items.summary: Introduces Student-Aware Teaching, where a stronger LLM builds a learner model of a fixed LLM agent to teach it skills within a constrained harness.
items.why: Points to teacher-side adaptation for agents with fixed tool and action-budget limits, relevant to agent skill transfer design.

items.title: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
items.summary: Proposes a language-grounded hierarchical reinforcement learning framework to coordinate multiple heterogeneous robots in simulated search and rescue operations.

items.title: AI Alignment Is Neither Solvable nor Sufficient
items.summary: Position paper argues that AI alignment is ill-defined, unsolvable in concrete forms, and insufficient as a goal for ensuring AI benefits society.
items.why: Challenges the premise of alignment as a central engineering target, which may affect how safety goals are framed in product and policy work.

items.title: From Process Models to Composable Agentic Workflows: Combining BPMN, Agents and Enterprise Knowledge
items.summary: Presents Recursive Capability Composition, a BPMN-based approach that lets agents execute business processes and expose them as reusable Agentic Tools.
items.why: Combines explicit process orchestration with autonomous agent reasoning, a pattern relevant to enterprise workflow monitoring and maintainability.

items.title: Counting Under Disagreement: Dollar-Weighted Measurement, Selective Machine Labelling and Budgeted Human Review from Disagreeing AI Readers of Administrative Text
items.summary: Paper examines dollar-weighted measurement of administrative text labels using disagreeing AI readers, selective machine labelling, and budgeted human review, tested on US tax-filing grant purposes.
items.why: Gives statistical methods for estimating monetary totals when AI labelers and human readers disagree, useful for large-scale document measurement pipelines.

items.title: Reliability of Claude Code as an Agentic AI Grading System for Handwritten University Exams
items.summary: Study evaluates Claude Code, an agentic deployment of Claude Opus 4.6, as a grader for 60 students' handwritten university mid-term exams against expert human grading.
items.why: Provides evidence on agreement, consistency, and feedback accuracy for AI grading in education, a concrete reliability benchmark for similar deployments.

items.title: W-ISA: Transactional Execution of Weight-Space Intervention Programs
items.summary: Introduces W-ISA, a software instruction set and transactional runtime for applying and restoring weight-space interventions on pretrained language models.
items.why: Offers transactional, restorable parameter edits for model runtimes, relevant to teams running request-scoped model modifications.

items.title: Decisions by Discrimination: Differential Evidence for Medical Reasoning
items.summary: Proposes a differential-evidence approach to medical multiple-choice reasoning that focuses on features distinguishing correct options from plausible incorrect ones.

items.title: NCP: Verifier-Guided Optimization of Weight-Space Control Policies
items.summary: Presents the Neural Control Plane, a closed-loop system that synthesizes, evaluates, and versions weight-space intervention policies for a language model's execution.
items.why: Separates control policy from the inference data plane, a architectural pattern relevant to managing runtime model behavior at scale.

items.title: ExpertCrowd-SWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Expert-Authored Engineering Tasks in Unfamiliar Codebases
items.summary: Introduces ExpertCrowd-SWE, a benchmark of 100 expert-written multi-file engineering tasks across 87 open-source projects for evaluating coding agents in unfamiliar codebases.
items.why: Offers a more realistic benchmark for coding agents on maintainer-style change requests, useful for evaluating agent tooling choices.

items.title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
items.summary: Empirical study proposes an episode record that traces where errors enter, propagate, and are detected in long-horizon LLM agent trajectories, and which controls could catch them.
items.why: Gives engineers a framework for diagnosing root causes of multi-step agent failures rather than only labeling symptoms.

items.title: Towards Scalable Network-Based Interventions for HIV Treatment and Prevention via R2C-Agent
items.summary: Introduces R2C-Agent, an approach for network-based HIV intervention targeting using peer referral networks in place of expensive full contact-network observation.

items.title: F3-AGI v4.0: Bioenergetically-Gated Active Inference, Metaplastic Preconditioning, and Residual Program Synthesis for Sample-Efficient Abstract Reasoning
items.summary: F3-AGI v4.0 is a CPU-native neuro-symbolic and active inference architecture for few-shot abstract reasoning on ARC-AGI, aiming to reduce spurious programs.
items.why: It targets sample-efficient program synthesis without pretraining, a problem relevant to engineers building reasoning systems under limited demonstrations.

items.title: Agent-Guided Discovery of Exchange-Correlation Functionals with Physics-based Validation
items.summary: Researchers connect frontier LLM agents to a GPU evaluator via Model Context Protocol to discover exchange-correlation functionals, validated with physics-based checks.
items.why: It shows LLM agents proposing scientific models with validation against external evaluation, a pattern useful for building agentic discovery pipelines.

items.title: Do AI Agents need Preventive Care? An Epidemiologic Cohort Design for Agentic AI
items.summary: A paper proposes an epidemiologic cohort design for studying agentic AI, treating individual agents as members of a cohort to track behavior over time.
items.why: It suggests longitudinal monitoring of deployed agents, which may matter for teams evaluating agent behavior beyond fixed benchmarks.

items.title: Disentangling Multimodal Rotary Positional Embedding in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: A paper examines Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding in vision-language models, finding that assigning height and width coordinates to text tokens introduces spatial effects.
items.why: It highlights a positional-encoding issue in VLMs that could affect text-vision attention in models engineers build or fine-tune.

items.title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
items.summary: Veritas is a harness that automatically generates verifiers for agent tasks, using evidence headers, domain-rule libraries, and related mechanisms.
items.why: Automatically generated verifiers could reduce the manual cost of evaluating self-improving agent systems.

items.title: Multi-Stage Phase-Aware Self-Supervised Reconstruction for Multi-Echo Gradient-Echo MRI
items.summary: Researchers present MSPR-GRE, a multi-stage phase-aware self-supervised reconstruction method for accelerated multi-echo gradient-echo MRI.

items.title: A Technique to Model Product Information and User Reviews (MPIUR)
items.summary: MPIUR is a multimodal graph-based recommendation model that combines product descriptions, images, and user reviews within a unified framework.
items.why: It offers a unified approach to integrating text, image and review signals in e-commerce recommendations, relevant to recommender system builders.

items.title: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents
items.summary: A paper argues that no finite rulebook can certify every safe program, proving an impossibility result for gatekeeping AI agents' generated code.
items.why: It implies static rule-based gatekeeping of agent-generated code cannot be fully complete, so guardrails need layered design beyond fixed rules.

items.title: Online-Adaptive Fuzzy Cognitive Maps for Neuro-symbolic Financial Forecasting
items.summary: A neuro-symbolic framework pairs online-adaptive Fuzzy Cognitive Maps with LSTM networks for financial forecasting across regime shifts.

items.title: Living constitutions: Participatory alignment for sovereign foundation models
items.summary: The paper proposes participatory processes for creating constitutions for sovereign foundation models used in Constitutional AI post-training.
items.why: It raises governance questions for teams deciding which values and norms their own fine-tuned models should encode.

items.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
items.summary: SteerDistill is a quantization-aware distillation method that uses closed-loop teacher steering to recover task success in low-bit quantized LLM agents.
items.why: It addresses accuracy loss when quantizing agents to cut inference cost, directly relevant to teams deploying cheaper agent models.

items.title: SafeRoute-MAS: Coverage-Aware and Risk-Calibrated Message Routing for Multi-Agent Scientific Reasoning
items.summary: SafeRoute-MAS is a coverage-aware, risk-calibrated procedure that keeps or removes specialist messages in multi-agent scientific reasoning, reporting token savings.
items.why: It reports a token reduction in multi-agent message passing, which could lower costs for multi-agent systems.

items.title: When Reasoning looks like Hidden Understanding: How Chain-of-Thought Fosters Anthropomorphism, Perceptions of Epistemic Superiority, and Cognitive Deference
items.summary: A paper studies how chain-of-thought reasoning displays foster anthropomorphism, perceived epistemic superiority, and cognitive deference among users.
items.why: It suggests that exposing reasoning traces in products can shape user trust in ways product teams should account for.

items.title: The WoW: A Large-Scale World Knowledge Corpus for Full-Lifecycle LLM Training
items.summary: WoW is a large-scale Chinese world knowledge corpus built around an Educational Knowledge Graph for full-lifecycle foundation model training.

items.title: Nepali-English Code-Mixed Speech Recognition: Data Preparation and Adaptation of a Speech Foundation Model
items.summary: Researchers adapt the 449M-parameter SraVaani hybrid speech model on 172.8 hours of Nepali speech, extending its tokenizer for digits and symbols for code-mixed English.
items.why: It offers a practical recipe for adapting speech foundation models to code-switched, low-resource languages.

items.title: Agent Benchmarks Stop Ranking Before They Run Out of Tasks
items.summary: Researchers re-scored released runs of eight agent benchmarks and argue saturation stems from pass/fail measurement rather than the tasks themselves.
items.why: Suggests teams should use richer scoring than a single pass/fail bit when judging agent benchmarks, so rankings stay informative longer.

items.title: Darmok: Championship Cryptic Crossword Solving via Constraint Tightening and Resilient Orchestration
items.summary: Darmok, an automated system, reportedly reached superhuman performance on British cryptic crosswords and competed at the 55th Times Crossword Championship in London.
items.why: Shows an automated system handling ambiguous, compositional language puzzles at expert human level, though the text offers little on engineering details.

items.title: Benchmarking Vendor-Guided Optimizations on Edge NPUs: From NPU Only to End-to-End Performance. Extended technical report
items.summary: Researchers propose a benchmarking method comparing baseline, vendor-guided NPU-only, and vendor-guided end-to-end configurations across four edge NPUs and three vision workloads.
items.why: Shows edge NPU performance depends on the full deployment pipeline, not just hardware, so benchmarks should measure end-to-end results.

items.title: Transformers Provably Learn Graph Search: Training Dynamics and the Exponential Power of Depth
items.summary: Paper proves theoretical architectural requirements for transformers on graph path-finding and analyzes training dynamics and the benefit of depth.
items.why: Provides theoretical grounding on how depth affects transformer reasoning efficiency, though its practical implications for engineers remain indirect.

items.title: Towards Reliable VLM Judges: State-Conditional Invariance and Presentation-Aware Diagnostics
items.summary: Introduces State-Conditional Invariance and GridWM-Judge, a diagnostic benchmark testing whether vision-language model judges change verdicts for the right reasons.
items.why: Offers a way to test whether VLM-based evaluators are reliable, relevant for teams using models as automated judges.

items.title: Earth Embeddings in Environmental Remote Sensing
items.summary: A paper reviews Earth embeddings as a way to make multi-modal satellite observations more accessible for environmental remote sensing practitioners.
items.why: Suggests pretrained embeddings could lower compute and harmonization barriers for geospatial data work, though the text gives limited specifics.

items.title: Megrez: A Knowledge-Guided Agent for Formal Mathematics over MK Set Theory
items.summary: Megrez is a knowledge-guided coding agent for formalizing textbook mathematics in Rocq libraries built on Morse-Kelley set theory.
items.why: Illustrates how domain knowledge can make coding agents more reliable when building and extending large verified codebases.

items.title: DrugCoding: A Scientific Programming Agent for Drug Discovery
items.summary: DrugCoding is a scientific programming agent designed to plan drug discovery workflows, select specialized models, and execute computational tasks.
items.why: Shows agent designs for coordinating multiple specialized scientific tools, a pattern relevant to complex domain pipelines.

items.title: Benchmarking LLM Next-Step Recommendations with Knowledge Space Theory
items.summary: Proposes a benchmark using Knowledge Space Theory as a formal reference to evaluate LLM next-step recommendations, with a sample study of 2,400 responses.
items.why: Offers a formal, domain-grounded method for choosing LLMs in educational recommendation tasks rather than relying on generic benchmarks.

items.title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans
items.summary: Introduces GenEA, an agent representation for reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans using a multilevel state-space.
items.why: Relevant to embodied AI teams working on inferring human plans, though the practical deployment path is not described.

items.title: Topological Dynamics Under Non-Stationary Supervision: Persistent Homology of Neural Network Weight Evolution
items.summary: Study tracks persistent homology of neuron-weight point clouds in an MLP trained on Fashion-MNIST under correct, fixed, and per-epoch permuted labels.

items.title: SeqFold: Timestamp-Addressable Compressed States for User Action Sequence Backbones
items.summary: SeqFold proposes exporting multi-layer user states from a frozen long-history backbone as compact, timestamp-addressable representations for downstream systems.
items.why: Offers a serving-oriented approach to reuse long user-action histories without re-running the full backbone for each prediction target.

items.title: Agentic AI Meets Formal Verification in the Era of Agentic Hardware Development
items.summary: Invited paper surveys how agentic AI can advance hardware formal verification across specification, proof, and related stages of circuit design.
items.why: Highlights growing need to verify AI-generated hardware designs, a concern for teams adopting agentic chip development.

items.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
items.summary: AutoManifold is an agentic pipeline that automatically generates manifold embedding algorithms tailored to user-specified structural priorities for data visualisation.
items.why: Shows agents automating algorithm design for visualization, though the text offers limited detail on performance or availability.

items.title: Broad-Persistent Advising in Interactive Reinforcement Learning via Latent State Encoding
items.summary: Proposes Encoder BPA, which uses a latent encoder to retrieve and reuse stored external advice in interactive reinforcement learning.
items.why: Offers a refinement for speeding reinforcement learning with human advice, but its relevance outside research settings is limited.

items.title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents
items.summary: Researchers discuss benchmarks for autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization and present Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework for critical-path analysis and RTL rewriting.
items.why: Shows LLM agents being applied to hardware design workflows, with benchmarks for evaluating RTL optimization under realistic EDA flows.

items.title: Integrating Action Prefix Prediction and Alignment Across Modalities for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose Improved Predictive Representation, combining action-prefix prediction with anchor-based multimodal contrastive alignment for reinforcement learning.

items.title: Ceci n'est pas une pipe -- Toward a Symbolic Solver for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus Using Evolutionary Computation
items.summary: Researchers explore an evolutionary-computation symbolic solver for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus, an area largely absent from ARC-AGI contest entries.

items.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
items.summary: Researchers present URDF2Ontology, an LLM-assisted neurosymbolic framework that converts raw URDF robot files into grounded OWL ontologies for task reasoning.
items.why: Offers a way to add formal semantic context to robot descriptions, which could ease symbolic task allocation in robotics systems.

items.title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
items.summary: Researchers propose using LLMs to turn counterfactual edits for recommender systems into coherent human-readable narratives instead of long low-level edit lists.

items.title: Beyond Proxy Metrics: MLLMs as Human Surrogates for Explainable AI Evaluation
items.summary: Researchers investigate whether multimodal LLMs can act as surrogate human participants for evaluating explainable AI techniques.
items.why: Could offer a cheaper, more reproducible alternative to human studies for evaluating explanation methods, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: TreeAgent: Structure-Aware Memory Agent for Processing Long Hierarchical Data
items.summary: Researchers introduce TreeAgent, a structure-aware memory agent that segments long hierarchical data like API responses and HTML while preserving record structure.
items.why: Addresses fixed-length chunking breaking related fields in structured inputs, relevant to agents processing long API or web documents.

items.title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries
items.summary: Researchers use Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling to study neuron-level organization of domain specialization in Mixture-of-Experts language models.
items.why: Clarifies whether MoE expert specialization reflects domains or token patterns, informing how engineers interpret and debug MoE models.

items.title: Personalized Memory Rubrics: Learning What to Remember per User via Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment
items.summary: Researchers propose Personalized Memory Rubrics, using rubric-guided credit assignment to learn per-user memory update policies for long-horizon personalized agents.
items.why: Targets the problem of coarse terminal-only feedback in training agent memory updates, relevant to building personalized assistants.

items.title: Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs
items.summary: Researchers introduce Hx2Dx, a multimodal arena that evaluates LLMs on conversational clinical reasoning, where diagnosis requires iterative history-taking rather than curated vignettes.
items.why: Highlights that static diagnostic benchmarks miss the inquiry process, a gap relevant to evaluating LLMs in clinical settings.

items.title: BARS: Budget-Aware Sequential Sampling with Refusal for Majority Identification under Unknown Distributions
items.summary: Researchers propose BARS, a budget-aware sequential sampling rule with refusal for majority identification in LLM repeated sampling under unknown output distributions.
items.why: Offers a statistically certified early-stopping method for self-consistency sampling, which could reduce LLM inference costs.

items.title: Cross-Border Fulfillment Center Selection via Doubly Robust Estimation and Linear Programming
items.summary: Researchers present a cross-border fulfillment center selection model combining forecasting, doubly robust estimation, and linear programming, evaluated on e-commerce shipping corridors.

items.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Approach to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming
items.summary: Researchers propose solving the Lifted Bellman Linear Programming problem with the method of multipliers, learning coefficients via dual ascent for offline RL.

items.title: Joint Quantization and Dynamic Partitioning for Context-Aware Edge Vision Transformers
items.summary: Researchers propose an edge orchestration framework that jointly selects vision transformer partition points, quantization bitwidths, and placement across connected vehicles.
items.why: Addresses running vision transformers on vehicles under varying bandwidth and load, relevant to edge deployment engineering.

items.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
items.summary: Researchers find that concentrated bursts of attention head masking degrade multi-step reasoning in 8B LLMs more than budget-matched diffuse dropout on GSM8K.
items.why: Suggests that how attention faults are distributed matters for reasoning robustness, relevant to reliability testing of deployed LLMs.

items.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
items.summary: Researchers propose an affect-adaptive negotiation strategy using continual learning (CLIFER) to personalize facial valence-arousal perception in real time during human-agent negotiation.
items.why: Generic facial-affect models degrade across individuals, so continual personalization may matter for agents interacting with humans in varied contexts.

items.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
items.summary: A survey examines how self-improvement mechanisms for multimodal agents transfer, or fail to transfer, across four scenarios including reasoning, generation, GUI navigation, and embodied manipulation.
items.why: Self-improvement methods validated in one scenario may not carry over to others, which affects how teams adopt them.

items.title: Recurrent Modular Structure in Spiking Neural Network Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers introduce Community Recurrent SNNs, recurrent spiking networks partitioned into fixed-role communities, for reinforcement learning.

items.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
items.summary: Researchers introduce LM-SimBench, a unified framework, profiling dataset, and benchmark for evaluating LLM training simulators used to compare parallelization strategies.
items.why: Simulators can cheaply rank parallelization strategies before costly distributed runs, so controlled benchmarks help teams choose tools.

items.title: Multimodal Abstention That Preserves Acquired Correct Answers
items.summary: Researchers propose ReFrain, a method that adds abstention to task-adapted multimodal models while limiting newly lost correct answers.
items.why: Adding abstention to fine-tuned models can silently discard capabilities, so regression-controlled methods matter when deploying them.

items.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose evidence-linked memory for LLM agents so lessons are checked against their source trajectories, reducing memory-induced performance degradation.
items.why: Agents that follow incorrect or misread lessons can fail tasks they would otherwise solve, so verifiable memory affects reliability.

items.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution, which treats agent lessons as hypotheses and admits them into persistent state only after verification.
items.why: Writing unverified episode lessons into agent memory can store unreliable knowledge, so gating updates may improve agent safety.

items.title: CLADE: Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
items.summary: The CLADE paper addresses retrieval-augmented QA where retrieved passages are accurate but more coarse-grained than the question, proposing category-level answering from such evidence.
items.why: RAG systems may wrongly treat coarse but correct passages as insufficient, which affects answer quality and abstention behavior.

items.title: Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose a Cognitive Learning-by-Thinking framework mapping four internal mechanisms in LLMs onto computational processes.

items.title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
items.summary: A study compares spending a fixed inference budget on weight quantization precision versus averaging over answer-option reorderings in small Qwen3 local models.
items.why: Engineers running small local models can use these results to decide between memory savings and reducing option-order sensitivity.

items.title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
items.summary: Researchers propose decoding with top 4 bits of 8-bit weights and re-running uncertain steps at 8 bits, using simulated quantization on Qwen3-0.6B and GSM8K.
items.why: Escalating precision only on uncertain steps could cut weight bytes read per token for local inference, a cost-relevant tradeoff.

items.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers evaluate whether five LLMs can generate formal partially observable stochastic game world models from natural-language scenarios, using a 44-scenario benchmark.
items.why: Mechanically valid generated models may still misrepresent the intended decision problem, which matters for verification workflows.

items.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
items.summary: Re-Search introduces a two-player Twenty Questions-style game in which models must rediscover a paper's core idea, built from 200 ICML 2026 papers.
items.why: The benchmark exposes how LLMs search the research-idea space step by step, which shows where ideation progress stalls.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.summary: ReTrace converts a natural-language SOP and logged agent runs into a reusable workflow where code, not an LLM, selects each next step.
items.why: Code-driven step selection could reduce latency and cost for repetitive business process automation with agents.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.summary: A three-phase study compares three evaluation frameworks for enterprise LLM analytics agents, covering harness stability, failure detection, and discovery.
items.why: Evaluation method choice affects whether teams reliably catch failures in multi-tool enterprise agent workflows.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.summary: Researchers propose Contrastive Discovery, which has LLM agents test a question against mutually exclusive competing explanations rather than a hypothesis against its negation.
items.why: It offers engineers a way to design discovery agents that identify which alternative evidence supports, not just that a claim is unlikely.

items.title: Data augmentation using generative networks to identify dementia
items.summary: A 2020 arXiv paper explores using generative models for data augmentation to train more robust dementia classifiers on small medical datasets.

items.title: Causal Time Series Modeling of Supraglacial Lake Evolution in Greenland under Distribution Shift
items.summary: Researchers present RIC-TSC, a causal time-series classification framework for modeling Greenland supraglacial lake evolution under distribution shift.

items.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose textual response-aware guidance to improve zero-shot adversarial robustness of vision-language models during adversarial fine-tuning.
items.why: Adversarial robustness for VLMs matters for deployments relying on zero-shot generalization, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: AFNO: Universal Certifiably-Arbitrage-Free Operator Learning Framework for European Call-Price Surfaces
items.summary: Researchers introduce AFNO, a neural operator framework that certifiably guarantees static no-arbitrage when predicting European call-price surfaces.
items.why: Standard neural operators can produce negative PnL in trading tasks, so guaranteed arbitrage-free outputs matter for quantitative finance systems.

items.title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
items.summary: Researchers propose Step-Aware Decoding, which flags anomalous denoising steps via entropy spikes to reduce hallucinations in multimodal diffusion language models.
items.why: It suggests a training-free decoding fix for hallucinations in diffusion-based multimodal models, relevant to teams deploying them.

items.title: SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer
items.summary: Researchers introduce SELD, a training-free, label-free detector for silent evidence loss, where context compression removes key evidence while answers stay unchanged.
items.why: Compressed contexts can silently drop evidence that downstream models rely on, a risk for pipelines that reuse compressed context.

items.title: Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation
items.summary: A paper argues that clinician edits to LLM clinical documentation can supply training signal, but many edits add unsupported information and need filtering.
items.why: Over 45% of edits in the reported deployment data add unsupported content, so raw edit logs need filtering before training.

items.title: Brasilidade: Measuring Brazilian Identity for Large Language Models
items.summary: Researchers release Brasilidade, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on Brazilian Portuguese language nuances, starting with its first domain of tasks.
items.why: It finds model size alone does not determine performance, so teams serving Portuguese users should benchmark locally rather than assume scale wins.

items.title: M\"obius Interaction Filtering: Order-Selective Spectral Regularization for Multimodal Humor Detection
items.summary: Researchers propose Möbius Interaction Filtering, an order-selective spectral regularization method for multimodal humor detection across language, audio, and visual inputs.

items.title: Token Importance-Aware Semantic Communication Enabled Robust Video Transmission
items.summary: Researchers propose Ti-SemCom, a token importance-aware semantic communication framework for bandwidth-efficient and robust wireless video transmission.
items.why: Prioritizing communication-relevant tokens could help video streaming over constrained wireless links, though the text gives few performance details.

items.title: When Proofs Are Abundant, What Is a Paper For?
items.summary: An essay argues that as AI makes formally verified proofs cheap, a research paper's value lies in its narrative, problem choice, reasoning, and community critique.
items.why: As verified results get cheap, teams evaluating AI-generated research should weigh reasoning and justification, not just correctness.

items.title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
items.summary: Researchers propose predictive surprise as a self-grounding concept bottleneck for interpretable time-series classification that can abstain when evidence is weak.
items.why: Interpretable, abstaining time-series classifiers matter for risk-sensitive deployments, though the text gives few implementation details.

items.title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation
items.summary: Researchers propose ADIndex, a layer-adaptive sparse attention indexing method using group-level distillation to cut indexer latency in DeepSeek Sparse Attention.
items.why: The indexer can take over 50% of prefill GPU time at long context lengths, so cutting it directly targets long-context inference cost.

items.title: Trajectory-Regularized Distribution Distillation for One-Step Generation
items.summary: Researchers propose trajectory-regularized distribution distillation (TRD), combining distribution and trajectory supervision to distill flow matching models into one-step generators.
items.why: It targets a known tradeoff in one-step distillation, where trajectory methods degrade at small sampling budgets, relevant to faster generative inference.

items.title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
items.summary: MADSNet, a multi-scale axial-attentive dense spiking network, is proposed to reconstruct images from spike camera streams with improved fidelity over shallow SNN methods.
items.why: It suggests spiking networks may narrow the fidelity gap with ANNs for efficient high-speed vision on low-power hardware.

items.title: ICLayout-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Custom Circuit Layout Design
items.summary: ICLayout-Bench is a benchmark evaluating LLM agents that use EDA tools to build and optimize GDSII custom circuit layouts from netlists.
items.why: It offers a measured baseline for whether LLM agents can handle physical chip layout work beyond schematic-level tasks.

items.title: Third Eye: Beyond Immediate Gains in Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Third Eye tests whether a self-update that helps immediately still helps after further native model updates, across five 3-8B backbones on math and code.
items.why: It finds immediate gains from self-improvement can be misleading, which matters for anyone deploying self-updating models.

items.title: Specializing Meta Multi-Objectivization as Baseline for Software Engineering Optimization
items.summary: The paper studies specializing Meta Multi-Objectivization, an auxiliary-objective method for escaping local optima, as a baseline for software engineering optimization problems.
items.why: It may help engineers tune search-based SE optimizers, though the summary gives limited detail on results.

items.title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption
items.summary: TIB proposes a sample-wise tempered information bottleneck for multimodal attribution that does not assume image-text pairs are always semantically aligned.
items.why: Better attribution on misaligned multimodal data could improve model interpretability for vision-language systems.

items.title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
items.summary: PhysMoE proposes single-token coordinate representation and modality-decoupled routing in embodied vision-language models to speed up spatial grounding for robotics.
items.why: Lower decoding latency for coordinate prediction could matter for real-time robotic planning and manipulation.

items.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
items.summary: The paper uses path signatures from rough-path theory to encode execution traces, improving trace-to-program induction on Karel, List, and RASP domains.
items.why: It offers a new encoding approach for inferring programs from execution behavior, relevant to reverse engineering research.

items.title: Just AI Governance and the Forbidden-Boundary Principle
items.summary: A conceptual study proposes a framework for assessing whether AI decisions are justified across normative, data, model, and governance layers, with a forbidden-boundary evaluation rule.
items.why: It offers a structured governance checklist for deciding when AI should hold delegated authority, though it is conceptual and untested.

items.title: An Open Implementation Flow for the Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 that Runs in the Browser, Checked Byte for Byte Against ISE
items.summary: An open HDL-to-bitstream flow for Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 runs in a browser via Yosys and nextpnr compiled to WebAssembly, checked against ISE.
items.why: Open toolchains for legacy FPGAs reduce dependence on discontinued vendor software for hardware projects.

items.title: Compile-Gated Lean Proof Refactoring with Enterprise Agent Practices: A Model per Step under a US\$3 Cap, Followed by Programmatic Rewrite Rules
items.summary: A closed-track Lean proof refactoring entry reports a score of 86.31 on 60 problems at about US$166 total, using a model-per-step approach under a per-problem cost cap.
items.why: It gives a concrete cost-per-task example for routing different models across agent pipeline stages.

items.title: Repository-Context-Guided Image Understanding for Agentic Software Development
items.summary: A method uses repository context to help coding agents localize relevant UI elements and source files from degraded bug-report screenshots.
items.why: Coding agents often receive low-quality screenshots, so grounding localization in repo context could improve bug triage.

items.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: GTAGym is an environment and framework for evaluating and reinforcement learning agents on GTA V tasks, with a 103-task benchmark derived from main-story missions.
items.why: It provides a verifiable testbed for agent perception and control in complex 3D environments.

items.title: Code-Grounded Agentic Explanations for Static Analysis Vulnerability Findings
items.summary: The paper proposes keeping static analysis detection with the analyzer while using an LLM only to explain SAST vulnerability findings, based on a 20-participant study.
items.why: Separating detection from LLM explanation keeps findings auditable while addressing developers dismissing unexplained alerts.

items.title: Beyond the Document: Compiled Context and Governed Agents for Any Work Product
items.summary: The paper proposes Portable Agent Format packages that carry work products with compiled context, evidence, provenance, and rules for later agent interaction.
items.why: Packaging provenance and authorization rules with deliverables could matter for governed agent workflows, though evidence presented is limited here.

items.title: Continuous-Time Set-Transformers for Asynchronous WiFi-IMU Indoor Localization
items.summary: A continuous-time set-transformer represents asynchronous WiFi RSSI and IMU measurements as timestamped tokens for indoor localization without resampling.
items.why: Handling asynchronous, missing sensor streams directly could improve indoor localization accuracy in practice.

items.title: The Indic Token Tax in 2026: Measuring Tokenizer. Disparity and Its Cost for the Languages of India
items.summary: A study measures tokenizer disparity across nine public tokenizers, including GPT-4o and Sarvam models, for all 25 Indian languages in FLORES-200 and Hinglish text.
items.why: Tokenizers that need more tokens for some languages raise per-token API costs, latency, and effective context length for those users.

items.title: A Multi-Word Tokenizer for 204 Languages That Needs Fewer Tokens Than GPT-4o's, Including on English
items.summary: Researchers present Havon v3, a 262,144-token byte-level BPE tokenizer trained on about 200 languages, which reports fewer tokens than GPT-4o's o200k_base on all 25 Indian languages tested.
items.why: Lower token counts for non-English languages could cut serving cost and latency for multilingual applications, though results are from a benchmark.

items.title: One Temperature to Rule Them All?
items.summary: The paper analyzes when varying sampling temperature across samples helps pass@K inference and when a single tuned fixed temperature is sufficient.
items.why: It helps teams decide whether to add per-sample temperature schemes or keep a single tuned temperature for multi-sample inference.

items.title: ASPIRE: An Agentic System-Identification Platform for Iterative Reasoning and Exploration
items.summary: ASPIRE is a framework where an LLM agent selects and executes methods to build nonlinear system-identification models from measured data.
items.why: It shows an agentic workflow applied to engineering modeling tasks that traditionally need expert judgment.

items.title: Just Image Transformers with Late-Stage Pixel Refinement
items.summary: The paper proposes adding late-stage pixel refinement to latent-free Just Image Transformers (JiT) to improve image quality over pure x-prediction.
items.why: It addresses a known quality gap in latent-free diffusion training, which could simplify image generator pipelines.

items.title: Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: The paper proposes selecting successful reference trajectories via free-target optimal transport to improve on-policy distillation for multi-turn tool-use agents.
items.why: Better teacher references may improve training of tool-using agents by avoiding misleading supervision from incompatible successes.

items.title: DOBB: Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes for Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance under State Uncertainty and Heterogeneous Dynamics
items.summary: DOBB introduces dynamic oriented bounding boxes to make learning-based multi-agent collision avoidance robust to state uncertainty and heterogeneous dynamics.
items.why: Encoding uncertainty and agent capability into the safety geometry may make decentralized robot policies more reliable outside training conditions.

items.title: Autonomous Optimization of Numerical Algorithms by an AI Agent: Application to Atomistic Simulation
items.summary: AIOA uses an LLM coding agent in an improvement loop, guarded by verifiers, to optimize numerical algorithms in the ASE atomistic simulation library.
items.why: It demonstrates agent-driven code optimization with verifiers that the agent cannot alter, a pattern applicable to scientific software.

items.title: Everything in its right place: attention is a radio head
items.summary: The paper proposes that attention can emerge from synchronization of oscillators, reframing it as a Kuramoto-style process rather than a digital calculation.
items.why: It is a theoretical reframing of attention with limited immediate engineering impact beyond conceptual interest.

items.title: How Much of Your VLA Is kNN
items.summary: The paper shows retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks reaches 91.7% success on LIBERO without policy training, and analyzes nine VLAs.
items.why: It suggests high VLA benchmark scores may rely heavily on memorized demonstrations rather than generalization, which affects how teams evaluate robot policies.

items.title: AgentScript-Eval: Benchmarking LLMs and Agents for Code Generation in an Enterprise DSL
items.summary: AgentScript-Eval is a benchmark evaluating LLMs and agents on generating code in an enterprise domain-specific language for declaring agent behavior.
items.why: Enterprise DSLs are underrepresented in pretraining data, so this benchmark helps teams gauge LLM reliability for internal platform code.

items.title: Multimodal Road Closure Mapping via Cross-Modal Graph Attention
items.summary: The paper introduces a multimodal, multitask framework that classifies road closures and identifies affected road segments using cross-modal graph attention.
items.why: Automated closure detection could reduce manual map updates for navigation and logistics systems.

items.title: Structured Kernel Surrogate Models for Multimodal Attribution
items.summary: The paper proposes structured kernel surrogate models for cross-sample modality attribution, measuring how one modality in a sample affects learning on other samples.
items.why: Attribution across samples could help diagnose which data modalities matter in multimodal training pipelines.

items.title: XAI-Driven Confidence Estimation for OOD-Resilient Runtime Prediction
items.summary: LEX is a post-hoc explainability framework that estimates input-specific runtime confidence for ML resource management models under out-of-distribution inputs.
items.why: Per-input confidence could let runtime resource managers avoid catastrophic failures that a single global error margin misses.

items.title: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood
items.summary: The paper introduces a child-centric video benchmark for evaluating nonverbal social reasoning in early childhood interactions.
items.why: Existing multimodal benchmarks focus on adult conversation, so this highlights a gap in evaluating nonverbal social understanding.

items.title: Wrong the Same Way: Cross-Prompt Sharing Both Suppresses and Amplifies Reward Hacking in RLVR
items.summary: Researchers study how RL with verifiable rewards interacts with imperfect verifiers, testing whether reward hacking is inherited from base models or amplified by RL.
items.why: Clarifies when imperfect reward verifiers lead to reward hacking, which matters for anyone training models with verifiable rewards.

items.title: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement across Seven Open Reasoning Models
items.summary: Researchers measure how deleting reasoning history in multi-turn tool calling affects task performance across seven open reasoning models.
items.why: Shows that dropping reasoning traces when routing requests across providers may degrade multi-turn tool use, relevant to system design.

items.title: STAR: Semantic-Criticality Tiered Allocation of Radio Resources via Zero-Shot Learning
items.summary: STAR proposes allocating wireless radio resources by semantic criticality, protecting task-critical image pixels with higher fidelity in remote AI inference.
items.why: Offers a way to cut bandwidth use in edge-to-cloud vision systems by protecting only the pixels that affect answers.

items.title: Curie's Jarvis: Autonomous Robotic Chemistry Experiments from Printed Protocols
items.summary: Curie's Jarvis is a robot arm system that reads chemistry steps from a printed sheet and carries out experiments on a bench built for humans.
items.why: Shows lab automation that works from human-oriented materials rather than fixed scripts and fiducial markers.

items.title: Adaptive Residual Quantization for Memory-Efficient Temporal Action Segmentation
items.summary: Researchers propose adaptive residual quantization to reduce storage of frame features for memory-efficient temporal action segmentation in long videos.
items.why: Addresses storage bottlenecks in replay-based incremental video training, relevant to teams handling large video feature banks.

items.title: Off-policy Learning with Excursion Policies
items.summary: Researchers introduce excursion policies, which follow the target policy for multi-step stretches before reverting to the behavior policy in off-policy RL.
items.why: Offers an alternative to linear interpolation for trading bias against variance in off-policy learning.

items.title: MRFoundry: Knowledge-guided agent loops for end-to-end MRI research
items.summary: MRFoundry is an open-source package that connects MRI domain knowledge to AI agent actions, with project memory and output checks.
items.why: Provides a reference pattern for grounding research agents in domain knowledge and validation checks.

items.title: Train High, Ship Low: Efficient LoRA Synchronization for Distributed On-Policy Post-Training
items.summary: HiLo replaces LoRA adapter transmission with compressed gradient dissemination and local optimizer replay for distributed on-policy post-training.
items.why: Could reduce bandwidth bottlenecks when syncing adapters to rollout workers in distributed RL post-training.

items.title: PegasusAI Studio: Legible Cyberinfrastructure and Accountable AI Agents for Scientific Workflows
items.summary: PegasusAI Studio is an AI-assisted science gateway that lets agents run scientific workflows on shared infrastructure with per-user attribution and privilege limits.
items.why: Shows how agents operating on shared compute can be attributed to users and bounded by their privileges.

items.title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
items.summary: Researchers show theoretically that LoRA with Gaussian initialization and frozen A acts as stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, and propose rank-aware learning rates for federated LoRA.
items.why: Offers theory and a learning-rate method for federated fine-tuning on resource-constrained clients.

items.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
items.summary: ProTEUS is a mutation-resolved world model pretrained on deep mutational scanning data for in silico closed-loop protein evolution.

items.title: When Are Predictions Enough? An Evaluation Protocol for Frozen Expert Composition
items.summary: Researchers propose an evaluation protocol for combining frozen deepfake detectors, comparing feature combination with prediction combination across 21 DF40 detectors.
items.why: Shows how evaluation choices can change conclusions about whether combining features beats combining predictions.

items.title: Enforcing Axioms for AI Alignment under Loss-Based Rules
items.summary: Researchers treat alignment principles as voters over pairwise response comparisons and study enforcing axioms under loss-based reward model training.
items.why: Connects principle-guided alignment with reward model training objectives, relevant to alignment method design.

items.title: The AI Era's Lines of Code? A Case Study on What an Engineer's Token Spend Measures
items.summary: A JetBrains case study links five weeks of coding agent token spend to commits of 404 engineers, finding spend varies mostly between engineers.
items.why: Suggests token spend is a weak proxy for engineering output, a caution for leaders using it as a productivity metric.

items.title: The Dose Makes the Poison: Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Generative Drug Design
items.summary: Researchers propose exposure-aware evaluation of generative drug design, using physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling to assess candidate molecules at practical doses.
items.why: Argues that selecting molecules by predicted properties alone overlooks whether they are practical at real doses.

items.title: Stinging the Swarm: Extracting Attacker Intelligence from a Twin-Controller OT Honeypot
items.summary: Researchers present Talos, an inline gate that flags hostile LLM agent requests to industrial controllers and diverts them to a mirror-twin decoy to extract attacker intelligence.
items.why: OT and ICS operators facing autonomous agent attacks on fieldbus protocols get a concrete detect-quarantine-decoy design to study.

items.title: Bursts That Outlast Themselves: Persistent Degradation in Prefix-Cached Agent Serving
items.summary: A paper shows that bursts of traffic can push a prefix-cached vLLM agent-serving system into a degraded regime with low cache hit ratio and halved throughput that persists after the burst.
items.why: Engineers running multi-turn LLM agents on prefix caching may see sustained performance collapse after transient load spikes.

items.title: Placing LLM Lookup Tables by Per-Layer Prefetch Deadlines
items.summary: A paper proposes placing DeepSeek-V4.1's 203 GB of Engram n-gram lookup tables across memory tiers based on per-layer prefetch deadlines, and models the resulting slowdown.
items.why: Serving teams sizing host memory and GPU cache for large lookup-table models can use the deadline-based placement model.

items.title: Free Lunch Uncertainty: Sequence-Level R\'enyi Entropy from Particle Decoding for Adaptive LLM Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers show that sequence-level Rényi entropy can be estimated at zero extra cost from Sequential Monte Carlo decoding used for power sampling, for adaptive LLM reasoning.
items.why: It offers a free uncertainty signal for selective prediction and adaptive compute without the cost of multiple sampled completions.

items.title: You Don't Need Feature Learning to Do In-Context Learning
items.summary: A theoretical paper studies how rotation-invariant kernel machines learn the in-context linear regression task, using a spectral view of memorization versus generalization.

items.title: Inherited Weights: Measuring the Tokenization Premium and the Sovereignty Cost of Language Models for the Global South
items.summary: A paper measures a tokenization premium across 31 languages and 7 tokenizers and argues that fine-tuned models inherit vocabulary, knowledge, and license from a few base families, affecting sovereignty.
items.why: Teams building models or products for non-US and non-China markets should weigh inherited tokenizer costs and base-model licensing.

items.title: ForeSpark: Joint Draft and Verification Budget Scheduling for Parallel Speculative Decoding
items.summary: ForeSpark proposes jointly scheduling draft and verification budgets for parallel speculative decoding, reporting that drafting can consume up to 40% of step time under high load.
items.why: Inference-serving engineers can reduce wasted drafting compute at high load by adapting draft length per request.

items.title: Leveraging Psychophysical Attentional Distribution for Gaze-Augmented Reward Modeling
items.summary: Researchers propose a gaze-augmented reward model for RLHF that uses psychophysical attentional distribution from eye-tracking data as a supervisory signal.

items.title: Sharp Sample Complexity of KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: A paper studies the sample complexity of KL-regularized reinforcement learning, improving prior guarantees that scaled with the effective horizon to the fifth power.

items.title: Reasoning-Aware Relational Representation Learning for Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation
items.summary: Researchers introduce RaRe, a reasoning-aware relational representation learning framework for open-vocabulary scene graph generation to handle long-tailed relations.

items.title: Dark Matters: VAE-Aware HDR Encoding for SDR-to-HDR Video Reconstruction
