items.summary: Researchers introduce EquivFlow, an encoding for SDR-to-HDR video reconstruction that addresses dark-side collapse in the frozen VAE latent of latent diffusion models.
items.why: Teams using latent diffusion for video restoration may gain better HDR reconstruction by changing how signals pass through the VAE.

items.title: Developing an Operational Model for an Internet of Data Based Trusted Data Space for Vocational Education
items.summary: A paper develops a multi-stakeholder operational model for a trusted Internet of Data based data space for vocational education, covering value network, revenue allocation, and governance.

items.title: Massive Activations Confound Sparse Autoencoders
items.summary: A paper shows that massive activations can make up to 99.9% of activation variance lie along the first principal component, undermining common sparse autoencoder evaluations, and proposes a correction.
items.why: Interpretability researchers relying on variance explained or ablation damage to judge SAEs may draw misleading conclusions without this correction.

items.title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
items.summary: A study questions whether dense Monte-Carlo process rewards are worth their cost in GRPO, finding continuations alone take 91% of total training compute in their setting.
items.why: Teams training reasoning models with RLVR should account for the large compute overhead of dense process rewards before adopting them.

items.title: A Concept-Based Interpretable Framework for Clinical Text-based Prediction via Token-Concept Attention without Concept Supervision
items.summary: Researchers propose a concept-based interpretable framework for clinical text prediction using token-concept attention, without requiring annotated concept labels.

items.title: Metamorphic testing of learned AC optimal power flow surrogates reveals representation dependence
items.summary: Researchers applied thirteen metamorphic relations to learned AC optimal power flow surrogates and found every tested configuration violates at least six relations.
items.why: Shows that surrogate accuracy for grid models can depend on how the grid data is serialized, so single-encoding evaluations may overstate reliability.

items.title: Market-Conditioned JEPA: Learning from Unpredictable Market Shocks
items.summary: Researchers propose Market-Conditioned JEPA, a self-supervised model that conditions asset prediction on the realized market factor instead of treating market-wide shocks as noise.
items.why: Offers a modeling approach for financial time series that separates market-wide shocks from asset-specific signals, relevant to quant and ML teams.

items.title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
items.summary: PhyRubric is a rubric-based diagnostic framework that scores text-to-video outputs on physical commonsense by checking caption-specific principles.
items.why: Gives teams a more diagnostic way to evaluate video generation for physical plausibility than single subjective ratings.

items.title: Synapse-Control: Making Agent Experience Actionable with Lightweight Runtime Control
items.summary: Synapse-Control is an agent runtime whose lightweight control plane selects experience-based advice and decides when to send it, using a 1.7B classifier instead of large-model diagnoses.
items.why: Suggests a lower-cost way to reuse agent execution experience without adding large-model inference overhead to every retrieval step.

items.title: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference
items.summary: MOAI is a homomorphic-encryption framework for non-interactive secure transformer inference, aiming to reduce HE's computational overhead for LLM inference in cloud settings.
items.why: Addresses privacy for cloud-hosted LLM inference, though the text provides limited detail on measured performance gains.

items.title: Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: Researchers find on-policy self-distillation degrades under continued training due to a growing mismatch between the evolving student and its reference-conditioned teacher, and study this behavior.
items.why: Warns teams using self-distillation for LLM training that gains may reverse with longer training runs.

items.title: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
items.summary: Ego Guidance proposes SPAR, a model that uses action-free human egocentric videos alongside action prediction to improve robot policy learning on out-of-distribution tasks.
items.why: Suggests unlabeled human video can improve robot policies, reducing dependence on costly action-labeled robot data.

items.title: AURA: Auditory Spatial Intelligence via a Unified Representation from a General-Audio Encoder through Complete Alignment
items.summary: AURA uses a general-audio encoder, trained without spatial supervision, to handle spatial audio question answering, arguing a frozen codec retains spatial information.
items.why: Indicates a single general-audio encoder may serve both semantic and spatial audio tasks, simplifying multimodal audio architectures.

items.title: On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems
items.summary: The paper studies private knowledge retrieval and private inference for secure multi-agent LLM systems, addressing threats such as memory poisoning by malicious agents.
items.why: Highlights security risks like memory poisoning in multi-agent systems that teams deploying autonomous agents must address.

items.title: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits
items.summary: Researchers trained generative quantum eigensolver policies on IBM's Heron processor, with hardware in the training loop, for sample-based diagonalization of organotin hydroxides up to 70 qubits.
items.why: Demonstrates hardware-in-the-loop training of circuit generators at 70 qubits, a concrete data point for quantum chemistry workflows.

items.title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
items.summary: The paper shows that weight-space programming, where language models read and edit trained network weights, can be applied to EEG and ECG models to debug planted faults.
items.why: Extends weight-editing-by-reasoning to biosignal models, an early result with limited detail on generality.

items.title: DisasterAgent: An Evidence-Driven Agent for Verifiable Disaster Report Generation From Remote Sensing Imagery
items.summary: DisasterAgent is an evidence-driven agent that generates verifiable disaster reports from remote sensing imagery using perception-augmented tools.
items.why: Shows an approach to making agent-generated assessments verifiable through evidence, relevant to high-stakes agent deployments.

items.title: Softness is something you also need! Why compliance helps control: information metrics of a passive walker with compliant ankle
items.summary: A study of a passive walking robot with a compliant ankle uses information metrics to argue that compliance helps control.

items.title: Bridging Graph and Pairwise Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Inference from scRNA-seq Data
items.summary: The paper proposes combining graph-based and pairwise learning to infer gene regulatory networks from scRNA-seq data, addressing overfitting in graph methods.
items.why: Offers a hybrid modeling approach for bioinformatics GRN inference, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Relaxing Cross-Modal Correspondence for Multimodal Remote Sensing Pretraining
items.summary: SemPair relaxes cross-modal pairing in multimodal remote sensing pretraining from instance-level to class-consistent semantic pairs.
items.why: Suggests pretraining may not need exact paired multimodal data, potentially easing dataset construction for remote sensing models.

items.title: Swanada: Split-Encoder Capability-Routed Conformer CTC and Sub-30 MB On-Device Speech Recognition Across Twelve Scripts
items.summary: Researchers present Swanada, a split-encoder Conformer CTC speech recognition system that runs on-device under 30 MB across twelve Indic and classical scripts.
items.why: It targets browser and mobile runtime bottlenecks like storage quotas and unsupported ops, relevant to anyone shipping client-side ASR.

items.title: CASCADE: Constraint-Aware SCAffolded DEcomposition for Logical Anomaly Detection
items.summary: CASCADE proposes a constraint-aware, scaffolded decomposition method for logical anomaly detection using large vision-language models with few normal references.

items.title: MusicFlux: Flexible Conditioning for Text-Guided Music Generation and Editing
items.summary: MusicFlux is a text-guided music editing model that adapts in-context conditioning from image editing to handle long audio sequences.

items.title: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard
items.summary: PolyRoute releases a 12-language and code-mixed benchmark for typed-decision department routing, with labels produced by LLMs and baselines.
items.why: Engineers building multilingual support routing can use it to measure encoder behavior outside English.

items.title: Satellite Pretraining Is Not One Thing: A Matched-Pair Study of Generic and Earth-Observation Foundation Models for Scene Classification
items.summary: A matched-pair study compares Earth-observation and generic foundation encoders on frozen scene classification across five RGB satellite datasets.
items.why: It suggests satellite-specific pretraining does not always beat strong generic encoders for few-label land-cover mapping.

items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks: Methods, Frameworks, and Perspectives
items.summary: A survey reviews mechanistic interpretability methods and frameworks for deep neural networks across image, audio, and language domains.

items.title: Transparency Disclosures for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.summary: The paper argues frontier AI developers should disclose five indicators, such as third-party chain-of-thought access, to help preserve CoT monitorability.
items.why: Disclosure norms for CoT access could shape how teams evaluate and monitor frontier model reasoning.

items.title: Region-Wise Logit Fusion and Utility-Gated Refinement for Brain Metastasis Segmentation
items.summary: COMPASS-METS combines three nnU-Net configurations with structured probability assembly to segment brain metastases and resection cavities in the BraTS-METS 2026 challenge.

items.title: MicroBT: Centroid-Guided Synergistic Learning for Multi-Modal Micro Brain Tumor Segmentation and Counting
items.summary: MicroBT proposes a centroid-guided learning method for segmenting and counting sub-3 mm micro brain tumors in multi-modal MRI.

items.title: CAppleNet: A Coordinate Attention-Based YOLO11 for Real-Time Apple Stem Cavity and Calyx Detection
items.summary: CAppleNet, a coordinate-attention YOLO11 variant, is presented for real-time detection of apple stem cavities and calyx, with a self-collected 1,506-image dataset.

items.title: Domain-Invariant and Language-Model-Assisted Acoustic Side-Channel Attacks on Keyboards
items.summary: Researchers study acoustic side-channel attacks that infer typed text from keystroke sounds, testing generalization to unseen keyboards, users, and noisy conditions.
items.why: Shows keystroke inference may survive real-world conditions, a concern for teams assessing physical and audio privacy risks.

items.title: TAPCO-G: LLM-Guided Design-Adaptive Timing and Power Co-Optimization with Graph-Based Physical Priors
items.summary: TAPCO-G uses LLM-guided rule adaptation with graph-based physical priors to co-optimize post-placement timing and power in chip design.
items.why: Shows LLMs proposing optimizer rule changes in EDA flows, with physical estimators checking the effects on slack and power.

items.title: The Case for AI-Enabled Gate Monitoring as Farm Security in the UK: A PRISMA-Guided Review of the Evidence on Rural Crime, Livestock Predation and Farm Access
items.summary: A PRISMA-guided review finds thin UK evidence on rural crime and livestock predation and assesses the case for AI-enabled farm gate monitoring.

items.title: Tailoring Optimization Approaches with Domain Knowledge in Industry Process for Meta-heuristic Development
items.summary: The paper presents an industry process schema for developing metaheuristics and applies a genetic programming method to vehicle routing and project scheduling problems.

items.title: Chem World: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Physics-Aware Framework for Trustworthy Molecular Property Prediction
items.summary: Chem World is a benchmark integrating 17 public datasets with over 800,000 instances across 10 tracks for molecular property prediction, plus a physics-aware framework.
items.why: A unified benchmark with physics-aware evaluation helps teams compare molecular property models more reliably.

items.title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
items.summary: Researchers argue that AI coding harnesses, which connect models to shells and filesystems, need compositional security defenses because injected instructions can misuse dual-use binaries.
items.why: Coding agents with shell and network access create real attack paths, so permission design and architecture matter more than model-level safeguards alone.

items.title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies
items.summary: A paper proposes controlled taxonomy induction using tool-grounded LLM agents and runtime-adaptive policies to reduce omitted entities and invalid hierarchy relations.

items.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
items.summary: TransGHOST is a causal, reference-guided method for real-time reconstruction of tissue occluded by instruments in ophthalmic microsurgery video.

items.title: Specify Privacy Yourself: Assessing Inference-Time Personalized Privacy Preservation Ability of Large Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce ITP3, a task testing whether vision-language models can apply user-specified personalized privacy rules at inference time.
items.why: Personalized privacy controls for multimodal models could matter for products handling user images, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: A paper proposes improving coding agent memory by using on-policy distillation with pre-trained file operations for long-horizon tasks.
items.why: Agent memory management for long tasks affects how coding agents handle context limits, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: A Stage-Wise Explainable Pipeline for Arteriolar-to-Venular Ratio Estimation and Retinopathy Screening
items.summary: Researchers present a five-stage explainable pipeline that estimates arteriolar-to-venular ratio from fundus images and performs exploratory retinopathy screening.

items.title: Margin-Guided Token Credit for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: MCPO is a reinforcement learning method for verifiable rewards that assigns token credit based on the model's top-2 next-token probability margin instead of uniformly.
items.why: Changes how reward signals are distributed across tokens in RLVR training, which may matter for teams fine-tuning reasoning models.

items.title: Interleaving anatomical inspection and diagnostic reasoning for explainable radiology report generation
items.summary: ARIVE is a radiology report generation framework that interleaves anatomical inspection with diagnostic reasoning, supported by a 159,416-item multimodal dataset.

items.title: Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution
items.summary: A paper presents program-aided skill evolution for LLM agents, representing skills as patchable programs rather than natural language documents.
items.why: Treating agent skills as maintainable code rather than prose could make agent capabilities easier to update and debug.

items.title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
items.summary: A paper extends APEX to streaming video generation, using condition shifting to remove the need for a separate fake-score network in few-step distillation.
items.why: Reducing training memory and compute for few-step video generators could lower costs for teams building streaming video models.

items.title: MISO-BR: An Open Corpus for Misogyny Detection in Brazilian Portuguese
items.summary: Researchers release MISO-BR, an open, versioned corpus of 896 balanced Brazilian Portuguese social media texts annotated for misogyny detection.

items.title: Can KV Cache Be Reused Across Model Updates? A DeepSeek-V4-Flash Case Study
items.summary: A case study on DeepSeek-V4-Flash finds KV caches can retain task information across model updates without reproducing the updated model's behavior, with accuracy varying widely.
items.why: Teams hoping to reuse cached context across model version upgrades should verify results, since cache reuse can silently diverge in behavior.

items.title: HandsOnAid: Building and Evaluating an Offline First-Aid Assistant for Emergency Response Scenarios
items.summary: HandsOnAid is a 4-bit Gemma 2B model fine-tuned with QLoRA on 5,550 first-aid QA pairs, designed to run offline on phones for emergency guidance.
items.why: Shows a small quantized model can be fine-tuned for offline safety-critical advice, though evaluation scope is small (41 question-answer pairs).

items.title: Obscured Wildfire Flame Detection by Spatio-temporal Analysis of Smoke Patterns Using Frame-wise Transformers
items.summary: Researchers propose a frame-wise transformer that analyzes smoke motion patterns across video frames to detect obscured wildfire flames.

items.title: ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision
items.summary: ZoomGain mines gaps between global and zoomed perception in vision-language models to generate fine-grained visual supervision without manual annotation.
items.why: Offers a way to create fine-grained visual training data automatically, which could reduce annotation costs for VLM teams.

items.title: From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models
items.summary: A paper argues that the concept of bias needs a stated reference standard, proposing a critical grammar of positionality for evaluating large language models.
items.why: It offers a framing for evaluating LLM behavior without an implicit standard, which may matter for how teams define and audit model outputs.

items.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
items.summary: Researchers present Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover that verifies a committed integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence bit for bit.
items.why: Bit-exact verifiable inference could help teams prove which model produced an output, though the text gives no performance details.

items.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
items.summary: ProofCoder is an agentic system that uses LLMs to automate proof synthesis for software verification in the Rocq proof assistant.
items.why: Agentic proof synthesis could reduce the expertise needed for formal verification of critical software.

items.title: Model-Free Runtime Measurement of Task-Relevant Information
items.summary: Researchers introduce Acquisition-State Telemetry, a model-free architecture that monitors whether autonomous systems' information-gathering processes are functioning during operation.

items.title: Looking One Step Ahead: An Anticipation-guided Agent for Object State Readout in Videos
items.summary: Researchers propose LASER, an anticipation-guided agent that improves object state readout in videos by looking ahead to distinguish successive states.

items.title: Visual Similarity in Adult Word Extension and Artificial Word Learning
items.summary: A reanalysis of adult word-extension data finds visual similarity, measured with DINOv2 embeddings, is associated with how people extend object names.

items.title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
items.summary: Researchers propose VATC, a network traffic class that uses a reserved DSCP value to identify agentic AI traffic and demotes flows whose behavior contradicts their declaration.
items.why: Routers currently have no class for agent traffic, so verifiable traffic classes could affect how infrastructure prioritizes agent requests.

items.title: Dyship: Leveraging Acoustic Features For Speaker Relationship Classification From Dyadic Conversations
items.summary: Dyship compares five speech representations for classifying speaker familiarity and kinship in dyadic conversations, reporting up to 87.81% and 85.17% accuracy.

items.title: An AI Assistant for Automating Anti-Corruption Expertise of Draft Legislation Based on the TRACE Framework
items.summary: Researchers present an AI assistant that screens draft legislation for corruption risks using the TRACE framework, with an open benchmark built from Ukraine's anti-corruption agency conclusions.
items.why: It shows a human-overseen pipeline applied to legislative review, relevant to teams building high-stakes document screening tools.

items.title: Lilo: A Multi-Agent Conversational Sandbox for Children's Digital Communication
items.summary: Lilo is a multi-agent conversational sandbox where children practice handling peer conflicts in group chats, tested in an exploratory study with 28 children.

items.title: Achieving Robust Channel Estimation Neural Networks on Doppler effects by Designed Training Data
items.summary: Researchers show that designed training data can make neural channel estimation more robust to Doppler effects in high-speed wireless scenarios.
items.why: Training data design may reduce the need for online fine-tuning in wireless systems facing unseen channels.

items.title: Ninety-Six Ways to Measure a Scribe: Fragmented Evaluation of Ambient Scribes in Healthcare
items.summary: A review of 54 evaluation studies identifies ten evaluation dimensions and 40 distinct metrics for ambient AI scribes used in healthcare, noting no agreed standards exist.
items.why: Fragmented evaluation practices make it hard for healthcare leaders to compare ambient scribe vendors or evidence.

items.title: Forward-Value Discretization: Faster Stochastic Diffusion Sampling Without High-Order Approximation
items.summary: Researchers prove that higher-order approximations do not improve the first-order convergence of stochastic diffusion samplers and propose forward-value discretization for faster sampling.
items.why: Shows that raising approximation order will not speed up stochastic samplers, which may guide sampler choices for diffusion model inference.

items.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.summary: An analysis of 1,260,967 Chatbot Arena votes suggests that perceived declines in AI assistant quality may partly reflect rising evaluator standards rather than model changes.
items.why: Perceived quality drops may stem from evaluator expectations, which matters when teams interpret user feedback or human eval results over time.

items.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
items.summary: EngineAgent is an agentic system that automates enabling new LLMs in on-device inference engines by handling cross-layer dependencies across conversion, operators, and hardware backends.
items.why: Automating on-device model enablement could cut the recurring engineering cost of supporting new architectures on heterogeneous mobile hardware.

items.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose B3, a method that refines two blocks of tokens in parallel within one forward pass to speed up block-diffusion language models.
items.why: Parallel block refinement could reduce latency for diffusion LLMs, which matters for latency-critical deployments.

items.title: Causal Concept Explanations for Deep Neural Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce CCW-Net, a concept-based explanation method that uses interventional mediation analysis to test whether explanations are causally necessary or sufficient.
items.why: Causal checks on concept explanations could help teams certify autonomous systems rather than rely on correlational interpretability.

items.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
items.summary: Researchers stress-test four time-series foundation models on changing sensor sampling frequencies to measure how their behavior tracks lost information bandwidth.
items.why: Engineers deploying TSFMs on sensors with variable sampling rates can use these findings to judge robustness to frequency changes.

items.title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
items.summary: A paper compares Branch-and-Bound and A* exact search for resource-constrained project scheduling, linking their formulations and analyzing performance differences.
items.why: Clarifies when OR or AI exact search methods perform better for scheduling problems, which informs solver choice.

items.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
items.summary: A team describes its 9th-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge, using one vision-language-action model across 100 household tasks in OmniGibson.
items.why: It reports that the model was undertrained in 2025, a practical lesson on training budgets for robot policy models.

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.summary: Researchers propose EM-DETR, an example-based grounding approach for building a multi-domain foundation model for medical lesion detection from heterogeneous annotated datasets.
items.why: Shows an approach to combine inconsistently annotated medical datasets, a common obstacle for training detection models.

items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.summary: A study compares adapting the DINOv2 foundation model with task-specific training for medical image segmentation, focusing on performance at new clinical sites.
items.why: Tests whether foundation model adaptation generalizes beyond training distributions, relevant to choosing models for clinical deployment.

items.title: Identifying Macro Causal Effects in a C-DMG over ADMGs
items.summary: A paper addresses causal effect identification for macro-level effects in partially specified causal graphs, extending work to C-DMG over ADMGs.

items.title: Can Large Language Models Develop Gambling Addiction?
items.summary: A study finds that letting LLMs choose their own bet size or set profit goals amplifies gambling-like risk-taking, with effects persisting after controls.
items.why: Shows that giving agents autonomy over sizing and goals can drive risky behavior, relevant to designing LLM agents with financial decisions.

items.title: Accurate Predictions in Education with Discrete Variational Inference
items.summary: Researchers release what they describe as the largest open dataset of professionally marked formative assessments and use discrete variational inference to predict student answers.
items.why: A large open education dataset could help teams build more accurate adaptive learning systems in data-sparse settings.

items.title: Dynamic Mixed-Precision Routing for Efficient Multi-step LLM Interaction
items.summary: A paper proposes dynamic mixed-precision routing that picks quantization precision per interaction step, since some steps are far more sensitive to low precision than others.
items.why: Per-step precision selection could cut inference costs for multi-step agents without sharply reducing task success.

items.title: A Dynamic Survey of Soft Set Theory and Its Extensions
items.summary: A book-length dynamic survey covers soft set theory and its many extensions, including hypersoft, bipolar, and dynamic soft sets.

items.title: MMCOMET: A Large-Scale Multimodal Commonsense Knowledge Graph for Visual Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers introduce MMCOMET, a large-scale multimodal commonsense knowledge graph that extends ATOMIC2020 with visual grounding for each triple.
items.why: Visually grounded commonsense knowledge could reduce retrieval of visually misaligned facts in multimodal reasoning pipelines.

items.title: TACT: Mitigating Overthinking and Overacting in Coding Agents via Activation Steering
items.summary: Researchers propose TACT, an activation-steering method that detects and mitigates overthinking and overacting in coding agents during long trajectories.
items.why: Addresses agent drift in long software engineering tasks, a reliability issue for teams deploying coding agents.

items.title: Instrumental Choices: Measuring the Propensity of LLM Agents to Pursue Instrumental Behaviors
items.summary: Researchers introduce a low-stakes benchmark measuring how often terminal-based LLM agents pursue instrumental behaviors such as self-preservation against human instructions.
items.why: Provides a concrete test for whether agents violate instructions to pursue goals, relevant to evaluating agent safety before deployment.

items.title: Differentiable Learning of Lifted Action Schemas for Classical Planning
items.summary: Researchers propose a differentiable method for learning lifted action schemas and relations for classical planning from data.
items.why: Learning planning action models from data could reduce hand-written PDDL domain engineering, though the abstract alone gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Market Regime Council for Dynamic Credit Assignment in Multi-Agent LLM Decision Systems
items.summary: Researchers introduce Market Regime Council, an online credit-assignment method using exact Shapley values to weight specialist LLM agents for portfolio management.
items.why: It offers a principled way to attribute credit across multi-agent LLM systems and improve transparency of allocation decisions.

items.title: Towards end-to-end LLM-based censoring-aware survival analysis
items.summary: Researchers present LLMSurvival, a framework enabling unmodified LLMs to perform censoring-aware survival analysis on tabular clinical data via pairwise ranking.
items.why: It shows how off-the-shelf LLMs can be adapted to handle censored outcomes in tabular prediction, a common obstacle in medical modeling.

items.title: Can AI Agents Synthesize Scientific Conclusions in Health?
items.summary: Researchers introduce SciConBench, a live benchmark of 9.21K health questions to evaluate AI agents synthesizing scientific conclusions from systematic reviews.
items.why: It tests whether AI research agents can be trusted for high-stakes health conclusions, a key evaluation gap for deployers.

items.title: From AGI to ASI
items.summary: A report examines how AI might develop beyond human-level AGI along a continuum toward Universal AI and artificial superintelligence.
items.why: It is a conceptual policy and forecasting report with limited direct technical guidance for engineering teams.

items.title: Einstein World Models
items.summary: Researchers propose Einstein World Models, a blueprint for training LLMs to use visualised counterfactual imagery alongside language to improve reasoning.
items.why: It explores whether visual simulation can complement language reasoning in LLMs, though the abstract offers little on measured gains.

items.title: Forethought: Verifiable Reasoning from Neurosymbolic Primitive Programming
items.summary: Forethought is a neurosymbolic reasoning system built from a library of symbolic primitives, aiming for step-by-step verifiable reasoning in agentic workflows.
items.why: Checkable, symbolic reasoning steps could make agent tool-use easier to verify and cheaper than long test-time chain-of-thought.

items.title: SupplyNetPy: An Open-Source Python Library for High-Fidelity Modeling and Simulation of Arbitrary Supply Chain and Inventory Networks
items.summary: SupplyNetPy is an open-source Python library for discrete-event simulation of multi-echelon supply chain and inventory networks with disruptions and stochastic demand.
items.why: Engineers building supply chain or inventory simulations get an extensible open-source tool with reporting and disruption modeling.

items.title: TRACE: Business Rule-Grounded Reasoning Curriculum for Knowledge-Preserving Parametric Tool Retrieval in Enterprise LLMs
items.summary: TRACE proposes a two-stage curriculum for parametric tool retrieval in enterprise LLMs, aiming to preserve tool knowledge and speed up decoding versus beam search.
items.why: It targets two known drawbacks of parametric tool retrieval, knowledge loss and slow decoding, relevant to enterprise agent deployments.

items.title: Messier: A High-Resolution Corpus for Cross-Benchmark Agent Evaluation
items.summary: Messier is a unified corpus of 923,158 agent evaluation records spanning 30 benchmarks, 745 agents, and 11,891 tasks, with new runs on underrepresented domains.
items.why: A standardized, comparable evaluation dataset could reduce costly reruns when benchmarking agents across fragmented suites.

items.title: Probing the Origins of Reasoning Performance: Representational Quality for Mathematical Problem-Solving in RL vs. SFT Fine-Tuned Models
items.summary: Researchers probe internal representations of RL-trained versus SFT-trained language models to explain why RL improves mathematical reasoning.
items.why: Understanding where RL reasoning gains appear internally can guide choices between RL and SFT fine-tuning pipelines.

items.title: When Words and Bodies Disagree: Realizing Verbal and Nonverbal Mismatch
items.summary: Researchers study modeling verbal-nonverbal mismatch so virtual agents can generate body behaviors that differ from or contradict their spoken words.
items.why: It may matter for building more realistic embodied agents, though the abstract gives little concrete technical detail.

items.title: Learning Action Models with Conditional and Quantified Effects via Uncertainty-Guided Exploration
items.summary: OHCAM is an online method that learns action models with conditional and quantified effects by maintaining beliefs over hypotheses and selecting informative actions.
items.why: Learning richer action effects from limited interaction could make planning systems work in more complex environments.

items.title: Purin: A Biology-inspired Mechanism for Artificial Neural Networks
items.summary: Purin is a biology-inspired mechanism that adds synaptic efficacy modulation with time-interval abstraction to convolutional neural networks.
items.why: It proposes a drop-in way to model short-term synaptic changes in CNNs, though the abstract gives limited evidence of benefit.

items.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Agent Distillation across Models, Artifacts, and Harnesses
items.summary: A survey reviews agent distillation, extending knowledge distillation from model parameters to reusable artifacts and execution harnesses for LLM agents.
items.why: It maps how agent-level knowledge transfer could cut deployment costs beyond model compression alone.

items.title: Decide, Ask, or Defer: Clinical LLMs under Incomplete Evidence
items.summary: Researchers propose a DECIDE/ASK/DEFER framework for clinical LLMs facing incomplete evidence, and evaluate Qwen, Gemini, and GPT on 200 DDXPlus-based evidence states.
items.why: Clinical deployments need models that know when to acquire more information or defer, not just decide or abstain.

items.title: Bridging the Evidence-to-Execution Gap:A Reflective Agent for Multi-Objective Peptide Design
items.summary: Researchers introduce EASER, a reflective agent that links LLM scientific reasoning to sequence generators via a learned property interface for multi-objective peptide design.
items.why: Shows a method to bridge text-level reasoning and controllable sequence generation, relevant to agent designs in biology pipelines.

items.title: GAGR-Lab: Evaluating Joint Spatial-Geometric and Analytic Function Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers present GAGR-Lab, a benchmark framework for testing joint spatial-geometric and analytic function reasoning using game scenes and Rust trajectory execution.
items.why: Offers a structured way to evaluate whether models can turn spatial configurations into symbolic functions that satisfy constraints.

items.title: MSCR: Jointly Balancing Utilization Across Modalities and Discovering Synergistic Information
items.summary: Researchers propose MSCR, a multimodal learning method that balances modality utilization while discovering synergistic information during fusion.
items.why: Addresses modality imbalance in multimodal models, which can limit gains from cross-modal interactions.

items.title: MoveBench: A Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Sports and Health Coaching
items.summary: Researchers introduce MoveBench, a rubric-based benchmark for evaluating LLMs in sports and health coaching, covering exercise safety and personalization.
items.why: Provides domain-specific evaluation for high-risk fitness and health deployments where general benchmarks miss key requirements.

items.title: IECG: Weakly-Supervised Interpretability-Enhancing Foundation Model for Electrocardiogram
items.summary: Researchers present IECG, a weakly-supervised ECG foundation model that jointly performs diagnostic classification and abnormality localization without manual region annotations.
items.why: Could ease interpretability barriers for clinical ECG models by reducing the need for costly abnormal-region labels.

items.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents
items.summary: Researchers develop a decision-theoretic account of how language agents use stored memory from past experience, measured in units of avoided task loss.
items.why: Gives engineers a formal way to reason about memory storage, recovery, and revision costs in agent design.

items.title: TACS-RF: Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave Modules
items.summary: Researchers present TACS-RF, in which an LLM coding agent drives EDA tools like Cadence Virtuoso and Ansys HFSS to design a 240-251 GHz sub-THz transmitter.
items.why: Demonstrates an LLM agent semi-autonomously driving industry EDA toolchains for hardware design, a practical agentic workflow.

items.title: Scoped Semantic Invariance as a Foundation for LLM Reliability
items.summary: Researchers formalize LLM consistency as scoped semantic invariance over query equivalence classes, operationalized using knowledge graphs as semantic control structures.
items.why: Offers a framework for defining and testing consistency of LLM answers to equivalent queries within bounded domains.

items.title: Are Spiking Neural Networks Harder to Steal? The Role of Stochastic Encoding in Model Extraction
items.summary: Researchers study whether spiking neural networks resist model stealing attacks better than standard networks and identify stochastic encoding as the source of that resistance.
items.why: Suggests a possible low-cost defense for edge-deployed models, relevant to teams protecting models on constrained hardware.

items.title: Learning Where to Trust: Reliability-Guided Expert Routing and Velocity Gating for 3D Deformable Registration
items.summary: Researchers propose ReliMorph, a reliability-routed framework for 3D deformable image registration that couples match reliability with context selection and update strength.
items.why: Presents a technique for handling ambiguous correspondences in medical image registration, though the text offers limited deployment detail.

items.title: SpectRAG: Weighted Chunk Graphs for Token-Budgeted Context Selection in Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Researchers propose SpectRAG, a spectral graph-augmented retrieval method that builds weighted chunk graphs for token-budgeted context selection in multi-hop RAG.
items.why: Targets redundant and incomplete retrieval in multi-hop RAG under token budgets, a common production constraint.

items.title: Learning to Reason from Reference Samples Alone: Reinforced Adversarial Learning for Modern LLM Post-Training
items.summary: Researchers propose using a co-trained LLM judge that scores on-policy outputs against reference answers alone, removing the need for explicit verifiable rewards or reference traces.
items.why: Could extend post-training to tasks where correctness is hard to verify programmatically, reducing reliance on verifiable reward setups.

items.title: Low-Margin Branch Points in Deterministic LLM Deliberation
items.summary: Researchers audit a five-agent deterministic LLM committee under greedy decoding, finding that small internal interventions at low-margin tokens can redirect transcripts.
items.why: Highlights that exact replay does not guarantee robustness, which matters for auditing multi-agent LLM pipelines.

items.title: MAGAR: Multimodal Agents for GUI-Based 3D Mechanical Assembly and Minimal Rework
items.summary: Researchers introduce MAGAR-Bench, a 4,000-sample multimodal benchmark for GUI-based 3D mechanical assembly that separates assembly decision, atomic action, and minimal rework.
items.why: Provides a benchmark for evaluating GUI agents on recovery from incorrect assemblies, with rework measured by moved parts rather than actions.

items.title: FORGE: Fault-Oriented Rework Code Generation for Executable Interlocking Assembly
items.summary: Researchers introduce FORGE, a method for generating executable rework programs that repair faults in interlocking assemblies while respecting blocking dependencies.
items.why: Shows LLMs can find assembly faults yet still fail to produce executable repair code, a gap relevant to any LLM-driven industrial automation.

items.title: Kierston & KierstonBench: Simulation of Allentown, PA and Evaluation of Language Models in Crime Investigation and Surveillance Tasks
items.summary: Researchers present Kierston, a city-scale simulation of Allentown, PA, and KierstonBench, a benchmark testing language models on crime investigation and surveillance tasks against known simulated events.
items.why: Provides ground-truth evaluation for LLMs in surveillance and investigation, a sensitive use case where accuracy is hard to measure.

items.title: Combining Relevant Expert Knowledge Using Mixtures of Feedback Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
items.summary: Researchers propose applying a legal-theory relevance standard to select only relevant expert answers when mixing feedback fuzzy cognitive maps in neuro-symbolic systems.
items.why: Offers a way to filter knowledge sources by relevance, which may improve accuracy and scalability as knowledge networks grow.

items.title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
items.summary: CompressionBench tests whether autonomous coding agents can compress pretrained LLMs within storage limits, producing compressed weights and executable inference code.
items.why: Tests whether coding agents can handle model optimization tasks end to end, relevant to efficiency work and agent evaluation.

items.title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency
items.summary: Circe proposes a training-free way to evaluate LLM response correctness using internal component interaction consistency rather than output signals alone.
items.why: Offers a reference-free correctness signal from model internals, which could help teams assess LLM outputs without gold answers.

items.title: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
items.summary: AWS explains how to evaluate AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval evaluators matched to specific behaviors.
items.why: Engineers deploying agents get a framework for matching task completion, topic adherence, data leakage, and step-skipping checks to the right evaluator.

items.title: Apple has new Mac app coming to make running local AI models easy
items.summary: Apple is reportedly preparing a new Mac app that makes running local AI models easier.

items.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
items.summary: Researcher found about 35,000 Grok Build apps exposed publicly, leaking confidential information, some belonging to SpaceXSI.
items.why: Shows that AI coding agent deployments can expose sensitive data, so teams should audit access controls and secrets handling.

items.title: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder
items.summary: OpenAI acquired Odessia, a travel startup founded by Sonder founder Francis Davidson, and has not said what it plans to do with it.

items.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect
items.summary: New York's AI safety law is taking effect, requiring major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.
items.why: Companies building or deploying frontier models in New York now face registration, disclosure, and incident-reporting obligations with fines for noncompliance.

items.title: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO
items.summary: Each of Anthropic's seven co-founders plans to sell the same number of shares in its IPO, about $250 million each at the price range midpoint.

items.title: Oura to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625M
items.summary: Oura agreed to acquire AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625 million, weeks after postponing its IPO indefinitely.

items.title: The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it
items.summary: The Verge reports on espionage concerns surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and their implications for US leadership in the AI race.

items.title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
items.summary: PSI is building a business around AI-driven scientific discovery, using an unreleased Anthropic model to address a quantum computing question scientists have pursued for nearly two decades.
items.why: Shows frontier unreleased models being applied to scientific research problems, a signal for R&D teams exploring AI-assisted discovery.

items.title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
items.summary: Google announced Gemini Intelligence, bringing new features to more devices.

items.title: Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
items.summary: Trovata built autonomous treasury agents on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, using an RBAC-secured architecture for bank-branded AI deployments.
items.why: Offers a reference architecture for deploying role-based, secured autonomous agents in regulated financial workflows at enterprise scale.

items.title: The indie game community is in disarray over AI and Big Walk
items.summary: Some IGF jurors said they won't vote for games using generative AI in any capacity, and indie hit Big Walk's developer disclosed limited AI use during development.
items.why: Shows growing community backlash over generative AI use in creative work, which can affect how studios disclose tools and where games get recognized.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
items.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Meetings, which can draft plans, map timelines on a whiteboard, answer chat questions, and pull data from connected work apps during meetings.
items.why: Signals AI assistants moving into live collaboration with access to company apps, raising integration and data-access decisions for IT teams.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy: a timeline
items.summary: A timeline reports on an alleged affair between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, with possible national security implications.
items.why: The story concerns national security risk tied to the US-China race for advanced AI infrastructure, which may affect chip supply and policy.

items.title: How TCS built an agentic test orchestrator with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: TCS built an agentic test orchestrator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that turns requirements into governed tests for BFSI clients, cutting testing effort 88% in an internal benchmark.
items.why: Offers a concrete enterprise pattern for multi-agent test automation with per-tenant isolation, though the 88% figure is an internal benchmark.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock tokenomics data lake
items.summary: An AWS post describes building a centralized data lake that aggregates Amazon Bedrock invocation logs from all linked accounts into one queryable table.
items.why: Gives engineers a way to track prompts, token counts, model choice, and per-call cost across an organization's Bedrock accounts.

items.title: eBay appears to have shut the door on third-party AI agents
items.summary: eBay appears to have blocked AI agents, including Meta's Muse, from browsing its platform, according to a reader's report to The Verge.
items.why: Shows marketplaces may restrict third-party AI shopping agents, which could limit how agents access and act on commerce sites.

items.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
items.summary: Nvidia announced at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon that it is donating OpenShell to open source and expanding its open source commitment with new AI infrastructure.
items.why: Adds a donated open source project and infrastructure tooling for Kubernetes-based AI workloads, relevant to platform teams running AI factories.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature
items.summary: Google is releasing Gemini 4 Carbon to the public after a two-week preview with cybersecurity defenders, and says it is its strongest model with an agent swarm feature.
items.why: A new frontier model with multi-agent capabilities that Google positions against Anthropic and OpenAI, relevant for evaluating model choices.

items.title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips
items.summary: Google announced two new specialized TPUs aimed at confidential model training and greater memory capacity.
items.why: New accelerator options for confidential training and memory-heavy workloads could affect infrastructure planning and cloud cost choices.

items.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS
items.summary: Meta's AI assistant Muse is now available on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS, with voice, text, and dictation interaction.

items.title: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share to reach an implied valuation of $1.404 trillion
items.summary: Anthropic set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share, implying a valuation of up to $1.404 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
items.why: A listing at this valuation would mark a major funding and market milestone for a leading AI lab, shaping sector investment expectations.

items.title: We’re bringing Adobe’s creative and productivity tools closer to your everyday Google apps.
items.summary: Google and Adobe are integrating creative and productivity tools, including editing PDFs in Drive and using Adobe AI within Gemini.
items.why: Brings Adobe capabilities into everyday Google apps, which may simplify document and creative workflows for enterprise users.

items.title: After challenging Google’s Android with Cyanogen, its co-founder takes aim at Windows for AI era
items.summary: Cyanogen co-founder is launching Kora, a free Windows alternative aimed at users who rely heavily on AI models and agents.

items.title: Spotify’s AI DJ gets new voices, personalities, and an option for less chatter
items.summary: Spotify Premium users can now pick new AI DJ voices with different personalities or turn off commentary between songs.

items.title: Adobe is going all in on agentic AI
items.summary: Adobe announced agentic AI tools at its Max conference, including letting third-party AI agents access and change design files.
items.why: Shows creative software vendors opening design tools to external agents, which affects integration plans for creative workflows.

items.title: Hands-on with Ring’s new AI drone camera for your home
items.summary: Ring plans to ship a flying indoor drone camera, the Ring Drone Cam, on January 27th, 2027, priced at $249.99, per founder Jamie Siminoff.
items.why: Consumer AI hardware with autonomous flight raises privacy and security questions for product teams building always-on home sensing devices.

items.title: Ring, known for its doorbell cameras, launches a home security drone and an enterprise security robot
items.summary: Amazon-owned Ring launched a home security drone and a rolling robot designed to patrol and protect businesses.

items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
items.summary: Google Cloud launched Gemini for healthcare, aimed at unifying clinical data and automating workflows to reduce administrative burden.
items.why: Healthcare engineering teams get a managed Gemini offering for clinical data integration, though the text gives few technical details.

items.title: Cyberattacks threaten to make open source AI a little less open, Hugging Face exec warns
items.summary: Hugging Face executive Irene Solaiman warns that rising cyberattacks on open AI platforms could lead to tighter security restrictions.
items.why: Stricter platform security could limit open access to models and tools that developers rely on.

items.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, whose agents wrote three million lines of Lean proofs to verify Signal's core encryption.
items.why: Shows AI agents producing large-scale formal verification of production cryptography, a useful signal for high-assurance software teams.

items.title: Helping caregivers use AI in everyday life
items.summary: OpenAI Academy is offering free, hands-on ChatGPT workshops for caregivers in five U.S. cities to build everyday AI skills.

items.title: Meet the Sad Wives of AI
items.summary: A Wired article titled "Meet the Sad Wives of AI" was shared on Hacker News, drawing 71 points and 63 comments.

items.title: AI usage generates a fragile codebase
items.summary: A blog post argues that AI usage produces fragile codebases; it drew 133 points and 171 comments on Hacker News.
items.why: Engineering leaders may want to weigh maintainability risks when adopting AI-generated code, though the text offers only the headline claim.

items.title: Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT, letting businesses manage their information, see how they appear, and turn interest into action.
items.why: Businesses can now manage their presence inside ChatGPT, which may affect how companies handle discoverability and customer engagement.

items.title: Closing the AI guidance gap in education
items.summary: OpenAI shares lessons from its EMEA education partnerships and new ThinkYoung research on supporting teachers, AI literacy and independent learning.
items.why: Offers guidance for leaders deploying AI in education, focusing on teacher support and AI literacy rather than tooling details.

items.title: Fireworks AI security breach impacts Notion and their customers
items.summary: Notion disclosed a security incident involving third-party AI vendor Fireworks AI that impacts Notion and its customers.
items.why: Vendor security incidents in AI inference providers can expose customer data, so teams should review third-party AI dependencies and their safeguards.

items.title: Otter AI can now follow conversations across 30+ languages
items.summary: Otter AI added support for 27 languages and announced an upcoming feature that can follow conversations when speakers switch languages.
items.why: Expands multilingual transcription coverage for meeting tools, though the text gives no details on accuracy or availability timing.

items.title: Work at the Frontier: AI’s effect on freelance work
items.summary: OpenAI and Upwork research finds shifting freelance demand, new skill combinations, and larger budgets and more hours for AI-related projects.
items.why: Shows how AI is reshaping freelance hiring and skill demand, relevant for leaders planning contractor and talent strategy.

items.title: Don't Blame The Preferences: Examining The Emergence of Sycophancy in LLM Training
items.summary: An arXiv paper investigates where sycophancy emerges across LLM training pipelines, comparing preference alignment methods like RLHF and DPO with earlier stages.
items.why: Suggests that blaming preference tuning alone may be misplaced, which matters for teams choosing where to mitigate flattering model behavior.

items.title: Veterans' Mental Health Crisis Severity Annotation: Do LLMs Agree More Than Human Experts?
items.summary: An arXiv study evaluates 15 open-source and 10 proprietary LLMs against veteran subject matter experts on crisis-severity annotation of social media posts.
items.why: Tests whether LLM annotation is reliable enough for safety-critical mental health triage, a key question for anyone building such pipelines.

items.title: LoRazor: Trimming Adapter Execution for Efficient Multi-LoRA Serving
items.summary: LoRazor is an arXiv method that releases LoRA adapters early during decoding to speed up multi-LoRA serving with limited accuracy impact.
items.why: Targets the computation and memory overhead of serving many LoRA adapters on a shared backbone, relevant to multi-tenant inference costs.

items.title: AYO: A Safe and Privacy-Preserving Platform for Studying Children's Interaction with LLMs
items.summary: AYO is an open-source arXiv platform for safely studying how children and adolescents interact with LLMs while addressing privacy and consent.
items.why: Provides an open research tool for child-LLM interaction studies, a niche where direct observational data has been hard to collect.

items.title: META-IR: Meta-Introspective Reasoning for Adaptive Safety Alignment in LLM
items.summary: META-IR is an arXiv framework that uses meta-learning to adapt LLM safety alignment against jailbreaks under shifting adversarial distributions.
items.why: Addresses static alignment failing against evolving jailbreak tactics, a persistent gap for teams shipping safety-tuned models.

items.title: The Infrastructure Divide: Analyzing Community Stance on Data Center Development via Reddit
items.summary: An arXiv study uses an LLM-powered opinion-mining framework on Reddit to analyze community stance on AI data center development.
items.why: Shows how local opposition, which reportedly blocked or delayed about $64 billion in U.S. projects, shapes data center planning.

items.title: Homeopathic Learning: Diluting poisoned fine-tuning data can strengthen its effect
items.summary: An arXiv paper on homeopathic learning finds that poisoned fine-tuning data with little effect alone can create a hidden backdoor when clean data is added.
items.why: Shows that data-poisoning audits that check each dataset in isolation may miss backdoors that emerge from mixing datasets.

items.title: What Is the Value of AI-Involved Art? Evidence From a Juried In-Person Exhibition
items.summary: An arXiv study of a juried in-person AI art exhibition with 209 participants finds evaluators often willing to buy AI-involved art, with pricing tied to perceived value and effort.
items.why: Offers empirical data on how people value AI-involved creative work, though it has limited direct relevance to engineering work.

items.title: WorldMind: Test-Time Scaling for Visual Spatial Reasoning through Latent World Simulation
items.summary: WorldMind is an arXiv method that improves VLM spatial reasoning on perspective-taking tasks by simulating scene transformations in a latent world model.
items.why: Proposes a way to add active scene transformation to vision-language models instead of relying on synthesized RGB images.

items.title: DeepResearch RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Deep Research Report
items.summary: DeepResearch RewardBench is an arXiv benchmark for evaluating reward models and LLM judges on long, information-dense deep research reports.
items.why: Gives teams a benchmark for choosing automated evaluators for deep research outputs, where human review is costly.

items.title: AutoEMatic: Runtime-Adaptive Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Automatic Exponent-Mantissa Refinement
items.summary: AutoEMatic is an arXiv system that adjusts weight, activation, and KV cache precision at runtime for LLM inference using entropy and hidden-state update signals.
items.why: Proposes dynamic mixed-precision inference that could reduce serving cost, though the text gives no measured results.

items.title: Key Institutional Considerations for Designing Effective Independent Verification Organizations
items.summary: An arXiv paper examines institutional and policy design for independent verification organizations that evaluate AI technologies, especially frontier catastrophic risks.
items.why: Highlights governance questions around third-party AI evaluation that may affect compliance and audit expectations.

items.title: AVCORP: Identifying and Resisting Deception via Communication Theory and Theory of Mind
items.summary: AVCORP is an arXiv corpus of 5,000 annotated utterances from 250 Avalon games, mapping 37 deception tactics for training agents to detect deception.
items.why: Provides labeled data and reasoning traces for building LLM agents that resist deception from users or other agents.

items.title: Generative Active Learning for Label-Efficient Pan-Organ Ultrasound Diagnosis
items.summary: Researchers introduced EvoDiff, a generative active learning framework combining diffusion models with information-theoretic objectives and evolutionary search for label-efficient pan-organ ultrasound diagnosis.
items.why: It targets data scarcity and costly annotation in medical ultrasound AI, a practical concern for teams building diagnostic systems across centers.

items.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
items.summary: Researchers propose PISA, a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model LLM router, and PISA-E, an extension supporting ensemble routing, to balance response quality and inference cost.
items.why: Per-request routing between models could cut LLM serving costs for web services without sacrificing quality, which matters for infrastructure budgets.

items.title: Multi-GPU MoE Inference with Adaptive Expert Offloading
items.summary: Researchers present AdaOffload, a multi-GPU hybrid expert execution framework for Mixture-of-Experts inference that uses adaptive expert offloading to scale performance with additional GPUs.
items.why: Existing offloading systems fail to scale across GPUs, so this addresses a real serving bottleneck for large MoE models.

items.title: ProofDiff: Auditable Argument-Level Comparison of AI-Generated Mathematical Proofs
items.summary: Researchers present ProofDiff, a method for auditable argument-level comparison of AI-generated mathematical proofs, focusing on the route from hypotheses to conclusion rather than wording.
items.why: Formal verification cannot tell whether two proofs follow the same argument, so this offers a tool for auditing model-generated reasoning.

items.title: ScreenProof: Where Is This Screen Wrong? Finding UI Faults Without a Reference
items.summary: Researchers introduce ScreenProof, a target-free critic that boxes UI faults such as clipped labels and touching letters in phone screenshots without a reference design.
items.why: A reference-free UI fault detector could serve as a cheap first-pass check on generated interface pages before human design review.

items.title: CoRA-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation by Context Selectors Under Token Budgets
items.summary: Researchers released CoRA-Bench, a benchmark comparing context selectors such as BM25, dense retrieval, and LLMLingua-2 on evidence preservation under shared token budgets.
items.why: Context selection can drop evidence needed for answers, so the benchmark's task-dependent tradeoffs inform how teams trim long inputs.

items.title: Do large language models rank moral values? A transitivity test of moral competence
items.summary: Researchers test whether LLMs produce transitive rankings of moral values across pairwise trade-off choices, treating transitivity as a minimal necessary condition for moral competence.
items.why: Strong moral benchmark scores do not show consistent value weighing, which matters before relying on LLMs in decisions with moral stakes.

items.title: Adversarial Evaluation of Large Language Models for Patient-Friendly Radiology Report Summarization
items.summary: Researchers developed an adversarial framework using radiologist-validated term substitutions and impression removals to test six LLMs summarizing CT and MRI reports for patients.
items.why: Robustness results on clinical summarization show where LLM outputs can shift under small input changes, relevant to any healthcare deployment.

items.title: Restoring General and Improving Domain-Specific Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs Without Retraining
items.summary: Researchers propose SPECTRA, a training-free weight-level method that restores refusal behavior in fine-tuned LLMs by transferring the base model's refusal direction into the fine-tuned weights.
items.why: Fine-tuning can erode safety behavior even with benign data, and a retraining-free fix lowers the cost of keeping domain models safe.

items.title: Conformal Fair Decoding for Large Language Model Recommenders
items.summary: Researchers propose FairRec, an item-level decoding framework that controls semantic disparity across protected attributes in LLM-generated recommendations without needing model weights or full logits.
items.why: It offers a fairness control for LLM recommenders when teams only have API-level access, which is common in production.

items.title: TripleGrader: A Web-Based Platform Supporting Collaborative Triple Annotation with Quality Grading and Inter-Rater Agreement Assessment
items.summary: Researchers released TripleGrader, an open-source web platform for collaborative grading of knowledge graph triples on a 0-10 scale with inter-rater agreement assessment.
items.why: Teams building knowledge graph benchmarks get an open tool for quality grading and measuring annotator agreement.

items.title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research
items.summary: Researchers introduce SIRIS, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can judge when simulator limitations invalidate a recommended design in AI-driven systems research.
items.why: Engineers using LLM agents with simulators need to know when simulator errors change design decisions versus leaving them intact.

items.title: Evaluating classification and explainability in multimodal petrographic image analysis
items.summary: Researchers evaluate classification and explainability of the LITHOS dual-stream vision transformer for petrographic thin-section images using plane- and cross-polarised light.
items.why: The paper examines whether attribution maps reflect real mineralogical features, which matters for trusting vision models in scientific analysis.

items.title: IdealCache: Rethinking Cache Scheduling in Diffusion Transformers via Ideal Trajectories
items.summary: Researchers propose IdealCache, a training-free feature caching method for Diffusion Transformers that targets an ideal result rather than imitating the standard denoising trajectory.
items.why: Caching that avoids inheriting the reference trajectory's quality ceiling could speed up diffusion inference without losing output quality.

items.title: SituRecBench: Evaluating Frontier Models as Situated Recommendation Assistants in 3D Environments
items.summary: Researchers introduce SituRecBench, an interactive benchmark evaluating vision-language models as situated recommendation assistants that navigate and interact within 3D environments.
items.why: It tests combined spatial navigation, visual grounding, and multi-turn interaction, a capability gap for teams building embodied assistants.

items.title: MambaLoc: Lightweight Indoor Localization Using Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation
items.summary: MambaLoc proposes a lightweight indoor localization model using cross-modal knowledge distillation, aiming for accurate positioning on resource-constrained edge devices.
items.why: Offers a lower-cost alternative to Transformer-based Wi-Fi CSI localization, which has quadratic complexity that limits real-time edge deployment.

items.title: A Topological Encoder Decoder Framework for Temporal Graph Learning
items.summary: Researchers frame temporal graph prediction as an inverse topology problem, predicting a multiscale topological descriptor of the future graph before reconstructing edges.
items.why: Targets temporal graph forecasting where new nodes and edges appear, a case where edge-level prediction methods break down.

items.title: A Computational Map of the Disaster Mental Health Research Landscape
items.summary: Researchers used large language models to systematically map the literature on disasters and mental health indexed in PubMed.

items.title: Too Big to Inspect? Ethically Auditing Large Datasets Through Small Samples
items.summary: A paper proposes practical methods for ethically auditing very large training datasets by inspecting small samples rather than every item.
items.why: Sampling-based audits offer a feasible path for teams needing to check bias in web-scraped training corpora too large to review manually.

items.title: Tail-risk-aware Agent Safety: Constraining Tail Risks Across Multi-step LLM Agent Workflows
items.summary: Researchers propose tail-risk-aware safety constraints for multi-step LLM agent workflows, arguing risks propagate across dependent steps and need joint handling.
items.why: Per-step guardrails may miss how risks compound across agent tool calls, memory, and planning, so workflow-level controls matter.

items.title: TurnFlow: Benchmarking User-State Reasoning in Multi-Turn LLM Agents via Scene-Guided User Simulation
items.summary: TurnFlow is a benchmark testing whether multi-turn LLM agents track evolving user requirements and enforce changed constraints, using scene-guided user simulation.
items.why: Single-turn accuracy does not guarantee reliability in conversations; this benchmark probes state tracking that production assistants need.

items.title: Beyond Query Similarity: Safety-Conditioned Cache Routing for LLM Response Reuse
items.summary: Proposes safety-conditioned cache routing so semantic LLM response caches reuse answers only when safety conditions match, not just query similarity.
items.why: Semantic caching can serve unsafe cached responses when context changes; safety-aware reuse policies address a real cost-versus-risk tradeoff.

items.title: D-REAL: Acceptance-Length Optimization with Unbiased Gradients for Speculative Decoding
items.summary: D-REAL is a post-training method that optimizes speculative decoding drafters directly for expected accepted token length, using unbiased gradients.
items.why: Directly optimizing acceptance length could yield faster LLM inference from speculative decoding without changing the target model.

items.title: DiSARM: Diverse and Surprising Association Rule Mining with Large Language Models
items.summary: DiSARM combines association rule mining with LLMs to assess subjective interestingness, aiming to surface diverse and surprising rules during exploratory data analysis.

items.title: BunshinRL: Splitting Live Agent Workspaces for Memory-Efficient Agentic RL
items.summary: BunshinRL is an agentic RL rollout system that shares memory across environments, caches tool prefixes, and speculatively executes tools to cut rollout cost.
items.why: Reducing memory and tool-call latency in agentic RL rollouts could make training agents on persistent workspaces more practical at scale.

items.title: Decentralised Drone Swarm Formation under Silent Failures with ACO Pheromone Claims and PSO Tuning
items.summary: Researchers present a decentralised drone swarm controller combining ACO pheromone-based task claims and PSO flight tuning that tolerates silent failures and lossy radio.

items.title: Represented but Not Used: Value-Policy Dissociation in LLM Agents
items.summary: A study of Qwen2.5 models finds LLM agents can represent action values internally yet fail to use them in decisions, a value-policy dissociation.
items.why: Shows that inspecting internal representations may not predict whether an agent actually acts on its evaluated consequences, relevant to agent debugging.

items.title: PatternBloom: Empowering Agentic RAG with Externalized RL-Distilled Graph Patterns
items.summary: PatternBloom externalizes RL-distilled graph patterns for agentic retrieval-augmented generation, separating procedural reasoning patterns from retrieved content.
items.why: Externalizing reasoning patterns could help agentic RAG systems avoid plateauing as reasoning depth grows.

items.title: Sampling Is Not Curiosity: Why LLM Agents Should Investigate
items.summary: A position paper argues LLM agents should actively investigate and update their model of the environment, since sampling tricks do not change the underlying model.
items.why: Frames a gap between stochastic sampling and genuine exploration that matters for designing agents on open-ended research tasks.

items.title: TimeHF 2.0: Multimodal, Multivariate, and Multi-Region Collaborative Forecasting for Large-Scale Retail Supply Chains
items.summary: TimeHF 2.0 is a multimodal, multivariate, multi-region forecasting framework for large-scale retail supply chains that incorporates flexibly expressed business knowledge.

items.title: In Search of Lost Time: Temporal Competence in Large Language Models
items.summary: Researchers evaluate LLMs' temporal competence in four stages, finding models know time's rules from text but struggle to predict durations.
items.why: Suggests LLM agents that schedule tasks or budget reasoning time may need explicit timing signals rather than relying on learned notions of duration.

items.title: Seeing Isn't Enough: Unlocking Visual Reasoning by Bridging the Reasoning-Access Gap with TIGER
items.summary: The TIGER paper argues multimodal LLMs reason worse on images than on equivalent text, even when they read the text accurately, and proposes a method to close this gap.
items.why: Shows vision-language apps may underperform on image reasoning despite good OCR, so teams should test reasoning on images separately from perception.

items.title: Receiver-Resolution APS-PDP Maps for Wireless Channels: Benchmarking and Coarse-to-Fine Modeling
items.summary: The paper introduces UrbanADPSMap, a benchmark converting ray-traced wireless channel data into receiver-resolution angle and delay power spectra, plus a coarse-to-fine modeling method.

items.title: InfoOrgBench: Can Agents Turn Scattered Information into Coherent Hierarchies?
items.summary: InfoOrgBench is a 150-task benchmark testing whether agents organize scattered meeting, issue, and design records into correct hierarchies, scoring structure at every level.
items.why: Existing agent benchmarks miss higher-level grouping errors, so this offers a way to measure whether agents file records under the right owners.

items.title: Agentic discrete-event simulation for manufacturing system design: an open 3D simulator, a benchmark and an industrial case
items.summary: SimuLean is an open-source 3D discrete-event simulator built on Unity, designed so AI agents can build and study manufacturing models through domain-level commands.
items.why: Verified simulator semantics let agents generate manufacturing models without writing unverified simulation code from scratch.

items.title: An LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Modal Chatbot for Tomato Disease Consultant
items.summary: A LangChain and Streamlit chatbot using Mistral and Llama 3.2 diagnoses tomato plant diseases from text symptoms and images, designed to run offline.

items.title: Efficient LLM Adaptation with Forward-Only Passes
items.summary: The paper proposes forward-only LLM adaptation that uses SVD component activation statistics during inference serving to adapt models without backward passes.
items.why: Could let inference infrastructure double as a lightweight task adaptation path, avoiding separate fine-tuning compute.

items.title: Towards Identity-Preserving LLM Agents under Model Transition
items.summary: Across 5,760 compliance runs in 12 regulated domains, the paper finds that swapping an LLM agent's backend model can cause behavioral drift even when persona, memory, and rules stay identical.
items.why: Model upgrades can change agent behavior despite unchanged configuration, so operators in regulated settings should validate after any model swap.

items.title: DFT-Agent Bench: Scaffold Effects and Execution Provenance in Autonomous DFT
items.summary: DFT-Agent Bench reports results from over 200 Quantum ESPRESSO tasks evaluating LLM agents on autonomous materials simulation, including execution provenance audits.
items.why: Shows agent scaffolding choices and execution verification materially affect results in scientific simulation workflows.

items.title: SLA-Aware Task Offloading in the IoT Edge-Cloud Continuum: Class-Weighted Deep Reinforcement Learning Against an Exact Optimum
items.summary: A benchmark compares class-weighted deep RL for IoT task offloading across edge and cloud against exact dynamic-programming optima on small systems.
items.why: Shows how reward design for latency classes shifts RL offloading behavior, useful when tuning scheduling policies for SLA-bound workloads.

items.title: MMGraph-Agent: Agentic Multimodal RAG via Cache-Inspired Multimodal Knowledge HyperGraphs
items.summary: MMGraph-Agent is a unified multimodal RAG framework that organizes knowledge in cache-inspired multimodal hypergraphs and aims to cut construction cost and context limits.

items.title: The Delta Gap: Cellular World Models for Perturbation Response Prediction Are Far Harder Than Global Correlation Implies
items.summary: The paper shows that global Pearson correlation inflates perturbation-response model performance, with GEARS scoring 0.977 globally but only 0.076 on delta Pearson.
